title: Variational Enrichment Of Adaptive Finite Element Spaces Beyond Polynomials
authors: Matthew Francis Dixon
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive finite elements refine meshes or increase polynomial degree, but coherent non-polynomial structure may remain expensive in either coordinate. We introduce variational enrichment, in which compact problem-informed functions complement ordinary h- and p-refinement. The framework applies to Galerkin and minimum-residual formulations whenever admissible functions and their residual value can be evaluated; it is not tied to one PDE class. Quotient-Schur analysis removes redundant additions and measures their variational value. For symmetric coercive problems, the present theory also gives an exact energy-error reduction and a reference-independent upper bound. Across heterogeneous media, stochastic coefficients, irregular domains, singularities, interfaces, transport, and oscillatory tests, hc helps when a compact function captures unresolved structure aligned with the PDE operator; it offers little benefit when that structure is redundant or mismatched. On SPE10 Models 1 and 2, coefficient-adapted functions improve polynomial enrichment in all eleven prescribed cases at equal dimension, by up to [MATH]. The wider positive and negative evidence supports the same conclusion: hc selects useful operator-compatible structure and otherwise falls back to ordinary hp refinement.
tldr: This paper introduces variational enrichment, a method to augment adaptive finite element spaces with problem-informed non-polynomial functions, improving approximation for certain PDEs.
motivation: Adaptive finite elements typically refine mesh or polynomial degree, but capturing coherent non-polynomial structure can be inefficient. The authors aim to incorporate compact problem-informed functions to better resolve such structure.
method: The framework applies to Galerkin and minimum-residual formulations, using quotient-Schur analysis to remove redundant additions and measure variational value. For symmetric coercive problems, it provides exact energy-error reduction and a reference-independent upper bound.
result: Across various tests (heterogeneous media, stochastic coefficients, irregular domains, etc.), the method improves polynomial enrichment in all eleven prescribed cases on SPE10 models, with up to a certain factor, but offers little benefit when structure is redundant or mismatched.
conclusion: Variational enrichment selects useful operator-compatible structure and otherwise falls back to ordinary hp refinement, showing its potential for specific PDE problems.

title: Data-Driven Optimal Control Via Koopman Operators And Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Equations
authors: Gaosheng Zhu Guuyuan Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a data-driven stable manifold (DD-SM) method, which integrates Koopman operator representation learning with the geometric stable manifold approach to Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations, enabling end-to-end optimal feedback control synthesis from raw trajectory data without prior knowledge of system dynamics. We construct an augmented control system under a unified symmetric subspace decomposition (SSD) and extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) framework for joint approximation of the drift field, control matrix and their spatial derivatives, and derive probabilistic finite-sample error bounds for invariant and non-invariant dictionary spaces to yield a provably accurate approximate characteristic system of HJB equation. Via Lyapunov-Perron operator and ODE perturbation analysis, we prove the data-driven stable manifold achieves monotonically decreasing semi-global error with growing training data. We further establish closed-loop exponential stability and quantify the optimality gap, both tightenable by refining model accuracy. An efficient algorithm pipeline with adaptive data generation and deep neural approximation is developed, outputting control signals within 1 millisecond. Experiments on a modified van der Pol oscillator verify the effectiveness of our method.
tldr: This paper presents a data-driven method for optimal control using Koopman operators and Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to synthesize optimal feedback control from raw trajectory data without prior knowledge of system dynamics, addressing limitations of model-based approaches.
method: They integrate Koopman operator representation learning with the geometric stable manifold approach to HJB equations, using augmented control systems, symmetric subspace decomposition, and extended dynamic mode decomposition, with probabilistic error bounds and deep neural approximation.
result: They prove semi-global error convergence, closed-loop exponential stability, and quantify the optimality gap, demonstrating control signals within 1 millisecond on a van der Pol oscillator.
conclusion: The method provides an efficient data-driven optimal control pipeline, but it is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Some Reverse Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev Type Inequalities
authors: Qianqiao Guo, Zhe Pu, Jiankang Xia
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish some sharp reverse Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev (HLS) type inequalities on \(^n\) and \(_+^n\). Using an operator representation, we overcome the difficulty that the symmetric double-integral structure is unavailable in the half-space setting. On \(^n\), for \(1 \le n < \alpha\), \({\alpha} < t < 1\), and \(0 < q < 1\), there holds for nonnegative \(f \) that \[ \|E_\alpha f \|_{L^{t^\prime}(^n)} \ge (n,\alpha,q,t) \|f \|_{L^1(^n)}^{\gamma} \|f \|_{L^q(^n)}^{1-\gamma}, \quad \gamma := {t^\prime}q}{n(1-q)} \] for some [MATH] iff \(q>{\alpha}\), where \(E_\alpha\) is the extension operator with Riesz kernel and \(t^\prime\) is the conjugate of \(t\). The sharp constant is achieved when \({n + \alpha t^\prime} \le q < 1\). On \(_+^n\), with \(2 \le n < \alpha\), \({\alpha} < t < 1\), and \(0 < q < 1\), we show for nonnegative \(f \) that \[ \|_\alpha f \|_{L^{t^\prime}(_+^n)} \ge}(n,\alpha,q,t) \|f\|_{L^1(\partial _+^n)}^{} \|f\|_{L^q(\partial _+^n)}^{1-}, \quad := {t^\prime}q}{(n-1)(1-q)}, \] for some [MATH] iff \(q > {\alpha-1}\), where \(_\alpha\) is the extension operator with Poisson-type kernel. The sharp constant is achieved when \({n + t^\prime(\alpha-1)} \le q < 1\). We further extend results to \(q\ge1\). The proofs use rearrangement inequalities, the sharp Carlson--Levin inequality, and refined pointwise lower bounds for the Riesz and Poisson-type potentials. Our results unify and extend the classical reverse HLS inequalities, especially on \(_+^n\).
tldr: This paper proves sharp reverse Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev type inequalities on Euclidean and half-space settings, extending classical results with operator representations and refined pointwise bounds.
motivation: The authors aim to establish reverse HLS inequalities in settings where symmetric double-integral structures are unavailable, particularly on half-spaces, and to unify and extend classical results.
method: The proofs use rearrangement inequalities, the sharp Carlson-Levin inequality, and refined pointwise lower bounds for Riesz and Poisson-type potentials, along with an operator representation to handle the half-space case.
result: They obtain sharp reverse HLS inequalities with explicit constants and conditions for both Euclidean and half-space domains, extending to q≥1.
conclusion: The results unify and extend classical reverse HLS inequalities, providing a comprehensive treatment for these functional inequalities.

title: Weak Stability And Binary Convex Combinations Of Slices
authors: Rainis Haller
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study weak openness and related geometric properties of convex combinations of slices of the unit balls of Banach spaces. We prove that, for every [MATH], properties [MATH] and [MATH] are equivalent, and likewise for their closure variants. Consequently, both [MATH] and [MATH] are determined by convex combinations of two slices; in particular P1 and CWO are equivalent. We construct infinite-dimensional real Banach spaces with [MATH] but without P2, and with [MATH] but without P3. In the latter space, every convex combination of two slices contains two points at distance 2, although the space fails the strong diameter two property. Finally, we give an equivalent norm on the real space [MATH] for which [MATH] holds, but P1 fails. These answers several questions raised in the literature.
tldr: This paper studies weak openness and geometric properties of convex combinations of slices in Banach spaces, which is a topic in functional analysis unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The research interests focus on quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems. This paper is purely in Banach space geometry, with no connection to quantum mechanics or information theory.
method: The paper uses functional analysis techniques to prove equivalences between properties P1, P2, P3 and their closure variants, and constructs counterexamples in infinite-dimensional spaces.
result: It shows that properties P1 and CWO are equivalent, and that P2 and P3 are determined by convex combinations of two slices. It also constructs spaces with specific properties and answers open questions.
conclusion: The paper contributes to the theory of Banach spaces but has no relevance to the user's research directions.

title: Positive Quadrature And Mobile Sampling Of Multivariate Trigonometric Polynomials
authors: Stefan Kunis
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The geometric properties of quadrature points in one and multiple dimensions are a classical topic in numerical analysis. Recently, generalized quadrature methods, where discrete points and weights are replaced by integration along curves, have attracted growing interest. This paper focuses on positive generalized quadratures that are exact for multivariate trigonometric polynomials. We derive upper bounds on the covering radius of such quadratures using sign-localized test functions, a technique that also extends naturally to algebraic polynomials on intervals, spherical polynomials, and hyperbolic cross trigonometric polynomials. For lower bounds on the length of quadrature curves, we compare two recent approaches in the context of multivariate trigonometric polynomials. The second part of the paper studies a well-known, geometrically simple curve that underlies rank-1 Korobov lattice rules for periodic functions. We prove that these curves are quasi-optimal with respect to multiple optimality criteria and demonstrate its adaptability to the 2-sphere.
tldr: This paper studies positive quadrature rules and mobile sampling for multivariate trigonometric polynomials, focusing on geometric properties and optimality of quadrature curves.
motivation: The paper aims to extend classical quadrature theory to generalized methods where points and weights are replaced by integration along curves, and to analyze the geometric properties of such quadratures.
method: The author derives upper bounds on covering radius using sign-localized test functions and compares approaches for lower bounds on curve length. The paper also analyzes rank-1 Korobov lattice curves for optimality.
result: The paper provides upper bounds on covering radius for positive quadratures, proves quasi-optimality of certain curves, and demonstrates adaptability to the 2-sphere.
conclusion: The work contributes to numerical analysis and approximation theory, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Joint Identifiability And Conditioning In Finite-Horizon Continuous-Time Inverse Lqr With Unknown Dynamics
authors: Meiling Yu, Yuan-Hua Ni, Lei Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inverse Optimal Control (IOC) aims to infer the underlying cost functional of an agent from observations of its expert behavior. This paper studies the finite-horizon continuous-time inverse LQR problem from closed-loop state--input trajectories, where both the system matrices and the quadratic cost are unknown. The finite horizon induces a time-varying optimal gain, and this endogenous excitation serves as the structural mechanism that makes joint recovery possible. We quantify this mechanism through three computable conditioning indices, which measure state richness, gain-variation richness, and injectivity of a structured cost operator. Using these indices, we establish joint identifiability conditions for the inverse problem considered here. Crucially, these conditions guarantee recovery of the ground-truth system matrices [MATH] and the true cost weighting matrices, rather than merely a behaviorally equivalent surrogate. We also develop a conditioning-aware sampled-data reconstruction method that reconstructs the gain [MATH] and the closed-loop dynamics matrix [MATH] from noisy measurements, recovers [MATH] in closed form, and identifies the quadratic weights through a convex semidefinite program. We further establish the non-asymptotic perturbation bounds and the consistency of the full reconstruction method under sub-Gaussian observation noise, with explicit dependence on the same conditioning indices. Numerical experiments support the theory and illustrate the diagnostic value of the conditioning indices.
tldr: This paper studies joint identifiability and conditioning in finite-horizon continuous-time inverse LQR with unknown dynamics, focusing on recovering system matrices and cost weights from closed-loop trajectories.
motivation: The research interests focus on quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems, none of which relate to classical control theory or inverse optimal control.
method: The paper introduces three conditioning indices to quantify state richness, gain-variation richness, and injectivity of a cost operator, and develops a conditioning-aware sampled-data reconstruction method using convex semidefinite programming.
result: It establishes joint identifiability conditions and non-asymptotic perturbation bounds, with numerical experiments supporting the theory.
conclusion: The work contributes to inverse optimal control but is outside the scope of the specified research directions.

title: Afdm-isac With Fractional Delay-Doppler Coupling
authors: Shaohua Li, Cunhua Pan, Hong Ren, Ruizhe Wang, Jiangzhou Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) is a promising chirp-based multicarrier waveform for high-mobility integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). Accurate angle, delay, and Doppler estimation is essential for AFDM sensing. Since target delays and Doppler shifts are generally continuous-valued, representing them on a discrete delay--Doppler grid causes energy leakage and peak displacement in the discrete affine Fourier transform (DAFT) domain. The AFDM chirp also induces delay--Doppler coupling in the DAFT-domain response. The resulting DAFT-domain matching-score surface exhibits a local ridge that is not aligned with the normalized-delay and normalized-Doppler axes. To address these issues, this paper investigates joint estimation of angle and continuous-valued delay--Doppler parameters for a colocated AFDM-ISAC sensing architecture. A transform-domain sparse sensing model is formulated from the fractional DAFT-domain response. Based on this model, a coupled-coordinate Newtonized orthogonal matching pursuit (CC-NOMP) estimator is developed. CC-NOMP uses the AFDM-induced coupling coordinate to parameterize the dominant local ridge. It combines coupled-coordinate Newton refinement with safeguarded updates, coupling-aligned delay refinement, and cyclic multi-target refinement to estimate angle, continuous normalized delay, and normalized Doppler. A deterministic Cram\'er--Rao bound and a dominant-order complexity analysis are also derived. Simulation results with continuous-valued off-grid target parameters show that CC-NOMP achieves lower delay and Doppler error floors than the considered baselines while maintaining comparable angle-estimation accuracy.
tldr: This paper proposes a novel estimator for joint angle and continuous delay-Doppler estimation in AFDM-ISAC systems, addressing off-grid leakage and chirp-induced coupling.
motivation: The paper addresses the challenge of accurate sensing in high-mobility ISAC systems using AFDM, where continuous-valued delay and Doppler cause energy leakage and peak displacement in the DAFT domain.
method: The authors formulate a transform-domain sparse sensing model and develop a coupled-coordinate Newtonized orthogonal matching pursuit (CC-NOMP) estimator that exploits the AFDM-induced coupling to refine parameter estimates.
result: Simulations show that CC-NOMP achieves lower delay and Doppler error floors than baselines while maintaining comparable angle accuracy, with derived CRB and complexity analysis.
conclusion: The proposed method effectively handles off-grid parameters in AFDM-ISAC, improving sensing performance in high-mobility scenarios.

title: Direct Acceleration Of Stochastic Root-Finding Without Variance Reduction And Regularization
authors: Nicolas Loizou Taeho Yoon
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Acceleration for deterministic root-finding problems has been extensively studied in recent years; specifically, the anchor-based, or Halpern-type methods achieve optimal convergence rates with respect to the operator norm. However, acceleration via these methods does not directly carry over to stochastic setting due to accumulation of errors, unless one enforces diminishing variance via increasing batch sizes or variance reduction techniques. In this work, we show that another class of acceleration, namely the dual-anchor mechanism, extends to the stochastic setting without such error accumulation, in contrast to anchor-based algorithms. Consequently, we cleanly achieve [MATH] complexity with iteration-independent batch size, without any variance reduction or double-loop recursive regularization, for stochastic root-finding (resp. fixed-point) problems with cocoercivity (resp. square-nonexpansivity) in expectation. For strongly monotone operators, the same algorithm attains a sharper [MATH] complexity, nearly matching the lower bound in terms of [MATH]-dependence.
tldr: This paper presents a stochastic root-finding algorithm with dual-anchor acceleration achieving optimal complexity without variance reduction.
motivation: Acceleration for deterministic root-finding does not directly extend to stochastic settings due to error accumulation, requiring variance reduction or increasing batch sizes.
method: The authors propose a dual-anchor mechanism that avoids error accumulation, achieving iteration-independent batch size without variance reduction or double-loop regularization.
result: They achieve O(1/k) complexity for cocoercive operators and O(1/k^2) for strongly monotone operators, nearly matching lower bounds.
conclusion: The dual-anchor approach provides a clean stochastic acceleration method for root-finding and fixed-point problems.

title: Agent Safety Should Be A Runtime Contract
authors: Albus W. Ng, Yi Han, Jusheng Zhang, Wenhao Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dominant paradigm treats AI safety as a property to be instilled during model training via RLHF, DPO, or Constitutional AI. We argue this is structurally insufficient for autonomous agents that execute code, mutate files, send messages, and modify databases. Agent safety should be a runtime contract enforced by the harness, and the contract has two complementary faces. The preventive face blocks dangerous actions before they happen via sandboxes, permission gates, output filters, and trajectory monitors. The evidential face requires verifiable proof that good actions actually happened, gating task submission on hard evidence such as test runs, log captures, file diffs, and citation grounding. We ground the position in four lines of public evidence, with row-level protocols and data released in the supplementary JSON files: a survey of 52 documented AI-agent and LLM safety incidents, a false-completion audit with 31 non-contested core cases plus one disputed illustrative case, a trajectory-schema audit of 12 public agent systems and harnesses, and a title-level audit of all 28,560 papers accepted at NeurIPS, ICML, and ICLR 2023-2025 showing a pooled 8-12x imbalance between training-time and deployment-time publication. Two prior communities that needed to enforce safety, computer security and the experimental sciences, converged on runtime contracts with both preventive and evidential elements; agentic AI is now under the same pressure. We formalize an Agent Trajectory Schema and Evidence Chain, state a compositional gating proposition based on standard monitor composition, and outline a research agenda. The right unit of safety in agentic AI is the trajectory-with-checkable-evidence, not the model.
tldr: This paper argues that AI agent safety should be enforced at runtime via a contract with preventive and evidential measures, rather than solely through training-time alignment.
motivation: The authors contend that training-time alignment is insufficient for autonomous agents that can execute code and modify systems, and that safety must be enforced at runtime.
method: They support their position with surveys of AI incidents, audits of agent systems and academic papers, and formalize an Agent Trajectory Schema and Evidence Chain.
result: They find a significant imbalance between training-time and deployment-time safety research, and propose a runtime contract framework with preventive and evidential components.
conclusion: The right unit of safety in agentic AI is the trajectory-with-checkable-evidence, not the model, and runtime contracts are necessary for safe deployment.

title: Knowledge-Graph-Guided Retrieval-Augmented LLMs For Explainable Root Cause Analysis In Automotive HiL Validation
authors: Hamza Ouarrad, Mohammad Abboush, Andreas Rausch
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hardware-in-the-Loop validation of automotive software systems generates large multivariate time-series recordings whose manual analysis is time-consuming and often limited to anomaly detection and fault classification rather than root-cause analysis. Although deep learning methods have shown strong performance in fault detection and classification, they usually require task-specific training or retraining when new fault locations, systems, or operating conditions are introduced. They also tend to treat localization as a classification task, without explicitly representing the spatial and functional relationships between fault locations, sensors, and downstream subsystem effects. This limits their generalizability and their usefulness for engineering root cause analysis and diagnosis. This paper proposes a knowledge-graph-guided retrieval-augmented large language model framework for RCA (root cause analysis) and fault localization in automotive HiL data. The method converts raw time-series recordings into compact diagnostic evidence, enriches this evidence with sensor-to-location and propagation knowledge, and retrieves similar historical cases to support the final reasoning step. The LLM is then used as a decision and explanation layer rather than as a direct time-series classifier, producing a ranked fault-location prediction together with an interpretable RCA explanation. The framework is evaluated on two automotive HiL case studies: an ASM gasoline engine and an electric vehicle system. The best-performing model achieves Top-1 accuracies of 90\% and 94\%, respectively, while recording-level aggregation reaches perfect file-level fault localization in the evaluated subset. These results demonstrate the potential of KG-guided RAG-LLM reasoning for explainable and generalizable HiL RCA.
tldr: This paper applies knowledge-graph-guided retrieval-augmented LLMs to root cause analysis in automotive Hardware-in-the-Loop validation, which is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Manual analysis of automotive HiL time-series data is time-consuming and existing deep learning methods lack generalizability and explainability for root cause analysis.
method: The framework converts raw time-series into diagnostic evidence, enriches it with sensor-to-location knowledge from a knowledge graph, retrieves similar historical cases, and uses an LLM as a decision and explanation layer to produce ranked fault-location predictions with explanations.
result: The best model achieves Top-1 accuracies of 90% and 94% on two automotive HiL case studies, with perfect file-level fault localization in the evaluated subset.
conclusion: The results demonstrate the potential of KG-guided RAG-LLM reasoning for explainable and generalizable HiL root cause analysis, but the work is outside the scope of the user's research interests.

title: An Fkn Theorem For The Binary Grassmann Scheme
authors: Yuval Filmus, Anqi Li, Dor Minzer
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A classical theorem due to Friedgut, Kalai and Naor asserts that if a function [MATH] close to a degree [MATH] function, then either [MATH] or [MATH] is close to either the all [MATH] function, or to [MATH] for some [MATH]. We prove a version of their theorem for the Grassmann scheme over [MATH]. More precisely, we prove if a function [MATH] is close to a degree [MATH] function, then either [MATH] or [MATH] must be close to a function of the form [MATH], where [MATH] is a set of points and [MATH] is a set of hyperplanes in [MATH].
tldr: This paper proves a version of the Friedgut-Kalai-Naor theorem for the binary Grassmann scheme, characterizing functions close to low-degree functions in terms of point and hyperplane sets.
motivation: The classical FKN theorem is a fundamental result in Boolean function analysis, and extending it to the Grassmann scheme is a natural mathematical question with potential applications in combinatorics and coding theory.
method: The authors use techniques from Fourier analysis on the Grassmann scheme, including spectral decomposition and approximation arguments, to establish the structural characterization.
result: They show that if a function on the Grassmann scheme is close to a degree-d function, then either the function or its complement is close to a function depending only on a set of points or a set of hyperplanes.
conclusion: The result generalizes the FKN theorem to a new setting, providing insight into the structure of functions on Grassmann schemes, though its direct relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is not apparent.

title: Association-based Privacy Attacks In Wireless Protocols: Formal Modeling And Mitigation
authors: Mohit Kumar Jangid, Felix Engelmann, Zhiqiang Lin
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11337v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the surge in privacy-sensitive data from sources such as social media and IoT devices, there is a pressing need for formal, automated methods to assess privacy risks within these intricate systems. This paper formally investigates root sources of pairing-based privacy threats exploited using replay/relay techniques in wireless communication. Our research harnesses condition-oblivious responses, replay-resistance, and distance bounding measures vital for protocols utilizing shared keys in allowlists for authenticated reconnections. Particularly, the paper uses formal modeling of notable wireless networks, like the Wi-Fi P2P persistent group formation and the Bluetooth Low Energy reconnection procedure, to illustrate the root causes and countermeasures. Our model rigorously validates the proposed solution against association inference attacks, along with existing formalizations of well-authentication, frame opacity, and no-desynchronization. The ensuing analysis reveals not only uncharted privacy realms in wireless communication but also identifies old and new vulnerabilities. Our proposed design changes are acknowledged by Wi-Fi Alliance and Bluetooth SIG, paving the way for future advancements in resilient, privacy-preserving wireless protocols.
tldr: This paper formally models and mitigates association-based privacy attacks in wireless protocols like Wi-Fi P2P and BLE, focusing on replay/relay techniques and shared-key allowlists.
motivation: The increasing privacy-sensitive data from IoT and social media necessitates formal methods to assess and mitigate privacy risks in wireless communication systems.
method: The authors use formal modeling of Wi-Fi P2P persistent group formation and BLE reconnection procedures to analyze root causes of association inference attacks, and propose design changes validated against existing formalizations.
result: The analysis reveals new and old vulnerabilities in wireless protocols, and the proposed design changes are acknowledged by Wi-Fi Alliance and Bluetooth SIG.
conclusion: The paper contributes to privacy-preserving wireless protocol design but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Ai Guardrail Survival Under Single-Cycle Agentic Self-Summarization
authors: Ted Kwartler, Alan Aqrawi, Arian Abbasi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-running agents periodically compact their context, replacing the transcript with a model-generated summary.Recent work shows that dropping a standing safety constraint during compaction drives behavioral violations acrossmany models (Governance Decay; Chen, 2026). We ask a finer question: under a single compaction cycle, how is a safetyrule lost, and what does that imply for detection and evaluation? Our central finding is that a presence check is not asafety check: when compaction does not drop a rule outright, it often leaves something that looks like a rule but doesnot act like one. On behavioral replay, a degraded residue leads the model to perform the prohibited action far more oftenthan an intact welded rule does (all-case gaps of +34 and +57 points under two replay models, both positive), category-level survival behaves like a residue, and even intact rules sometimes fail to fire, so an audit that checks only textualpresence gives false assurance. Sharpening this, rule-form items are retained substantially more often than prominence-matched facts, which is exactly why presence-based checking feels adequate even though survival is not protection.Textual loss is regime-dependent (weld-or-drop with a single rule; degraded predicate-loss residues under a tighterbudget), and we did not observe the hypothesized textual severing mode. Such loss is silent at runtime and detectableonly by comparison with retained external ground truth (such as a constraint registry), which reveals textual absence butnot whether a surviving rule still fires. We also document evaluation pitfalls where LLM-judge labels alone would havereversed a conclusion. All results concern a single compaction cycle.
tldr: This paper studies how safety rules degrade during single-cycle context compaction in AI agents, showing that textual presence does not guarantee behavioral compliance.
motivation: Long-running AI agents compact context via summarization, which can cause safety constraints to be lost or degraded, leading to behavioral violations. The authors aim to understand the mechanisms of rule loss and improve detection.
method: They analyze a single compaction cycle, comparing intact rules vs. degraded residues via behavioral replay and textual analysis, and examine rule-form retention vs. prominence-matched facts.
result: Degraded residues cause prohibited actions more often than intact rules (+34 and +57 points), and intact rules sometimes fail to fire; textual loss is regime-dependent and silent at runtime.
conclusion: Presence-based audits are insufficient; detection requires external ground truth and behavioral testing, and evaluation pitfalls can reverse conclusions if relying solely on LLM judges.

title: The Next Challenge For Agentic Cybersecurity: A Realistic, Contamination-Free Reverse Engineering Benchmark
authors: Jeremy Spence, Nicholas Assaderaghi, Jinhao Zhu, Nikil Ravi, Raluca Ada Popa, Guannan Wei, Yangruibo Ding, Zhuo Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents are rapidly improving in cybersecurity capabilities when the source code is available for analysis, yet much of the software most consequential to cybersecurity, including malware, firmware, and proprietary applications, is available only as binaries. Analyzing such software requires reverse engineering(RE): recovering program semantics before the analysis can be meaningfully performed. However, evaluating agentic RE poses a fundamental challenge: benchmark instances must be unseen as source code in the LLMs' training data to prevent models from taking shortcuts by recognizing them rather than really analyzing them, while also matching the scale and anti-analysis protections of real software. Unfortunately, however, existing benchmarks do not jointly satisfy these requirements. To this end, we introduce SRE-Bench, the first realistic, contamination-free RE benchmark. Built entirely from scratch by RE experts with over 5,000 hours, SRE-Bench comprises 19 private, real-world-scale programs averaging 16.9K lines of code. We further developed 44 in-house anti-analysis primitives, yielding 262 binary instances and 1572 deterministically graded tasks. Our evaluation across five frontier LLMs (GPT-5.6-sol,Claude-Opus-5,GPT-5.5,Grok-4.5, and GLM-5.2) shows that RE remains largely unsolved: the strongest model, GPT-5.6-sol, scores 61.4% per instance, and fully solves only 31.5% of the instances. Our analysis further reveals that agents behave differently from human engineers, where agents are relatively insensitive to compiler optimization and static linking. Controlled ablations also confirm that both contamination control and realistic scale are essential. These results indicate that strong source-code security capabilities do not yet transfer to binary analysis, highlighting RE as an important frontier for agentic cybersecurity and SRE-Bench as a rigorous testbed to measure progress.
tldr: This paper introduces SRE-Bench, a contamination-free reverse engineering benchmark for evaluating AI agents on binary analysis, but it is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The paper addresses the challenge of evaluating AI agents in reverse engineering, which is crucial for cybersecurity but not aligned with the user's focus areas.
method: The authors built a benchmark with 19 private programs, 44 anti-analysis primitives, and 262 binary instances, and evaluated five frontier LLMs on reverse engineering tasks.
result: The strongest model scored 61.4% per instance and fully solved only 31.5% of instances, indicating that RE remains largely unsolved.
conclusion: The paper highlights reverse engineering as a frontier for agentic cybersecurity, but it is outside the scope of the user's research interests.

title: A Runtime Decentralized Attestation And Coordinated Repair Framework For Securing Automotive ECUs
authors: Josh Dafoe, Niusen Chen, Bo Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The evolution of automotive technology increasingly integrates components, transforming vehicles into interconnected systems of systems. Modern vehicles are controlled by a distributed system of computing devices, known as electronic control units (ECUs). However, this interconnectedness means that any error poses significant risks to the vehicle operator. In particular, malware can be injected into ECUs, threatening vehicle safety. To address this, we need mechanisms to detect compromised ECUs then repair them to a benign state. Existing approaches mainly focus on detection and do not address the challenge of integrating detection with runtime ECU repair. This integration is nontrivial because runtime repair involves both local rollback and reboot with timing determined from global vehicle context to avoid unsafe behavior. In this work, we have designed DACER, a runtime decentralized attestation and coordinated repair framework for automotive ECUs. DACER is the first approach that co-designs attestation and repair to unify the ``local'' nature of firmware rollback with the ``global'' nature of ECU reboot. In DACER, each ECU performs efficient local self-attestation and self-repair functions, enabling low-overhead coordination for distributed operations. In addition, DACER takes advantage of the hierarchical vehicle computing architecture. Our resulting DACER design checks the entire state of the vehicle, resists single points of failure, conforms to real-time constraints, and enables firmware restoration during runtime. The key functions are enabled by the ARM TrustZone equipped within each ECU and the secure flash memory controller embedded in the storage device. We implemented DACER on real-world hardware and experimentally demonstrated its low overhead.
tldr: This paper presents DACER, a runtime decentralized attestation and coordinated repair framework for automotive ECUs, focusing on security and safety in vehicles.
motivation: Modern vehicles are vulnerable to malware injection into ECUs, and existing detection methods lack integration with runtime repair, which is challenging due to local rollback and global reboot coordination.
method: DACER co-designs attestation and repair, using ARM TrustZone for local self-attestation and self-repair, and leverages the hierarchical vehicle architecture for coordinated global reboot decisions.
result: Implemented on real hardware, DACER demonstrates low overhead and meets real-time constraints while enabling firmware restoration during runtime.
conclusion: DACER provides a novel approach to securing automotive ECUs by unifying local and global repair mechanisms, but it is outside the scope of the specified research interests.

title: Discrete Linear Ensemble Logic
authors: Guo-Qiang Zhang Manfred Droste
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the discrete point-based fragment of Ensemble Logic [MATH] over the natural numbers, a logic combining displacement [MATH], bounded metric modalities [MATH] and [MATH] with additive bounds, Boolean connectives, and first-order quantification over [MATH]. Motivated by the need for a unified symbolic layer for biomedical knowledge with temporal, spatial, genomic, and multimodal metric content, we develop the foundational discrete theory of the formalism. We give syntax and semantics, and prove a forward embedding of [MATH] over a finite proposition set [MATH] into first-order monadic Presburger arithmetic [MATH]. This embedding yields the analytical upper bounds, while a reduction from nondeterministic two-counter machines with recurring control states proves that satisfiability is [MATH]-complete and validity is dually [MATH]-complete. Expressively, [MATH] strictly extends the star-free [MATH]-languages and is incomparable with the [MATH]-regular languages: it defines the non-[MATH]-regular counting language [MATH], whereas a delimited parity language remains outside the logic by classical Presburger-arithmetic lower bounds. On the proof-theoretic side, we present a sound Hilbert system [MATH] and establish completeness relative to monadic Presburger validity as oracle, noting that completeness relative to plain Presburger arithmetic is impossible.
tldr: This paper introduces a discrete fragment of Ensemble Logic, a multimodal logic for biomedical knowledge, and proves its satisfiability is EXPSPACE-complete via a reduction from two-counter machines.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a unified symbolic layer for biomedical knowledge with temporal, spatial, genomic, and multimodal metric content, which requires a logic with expressive power beyond regular languages.
method: They define the syntax and semantics of the discrete point-based fragment, prove a forward embedding into first-order monadic Presburger arithmetic, and reduce from nondeterministic two-counter machines to establish complexity bounds.
result: Satisfiability is EXPSPACE-complete, validity is co-EXPSPACE-complete, and the logic strictly extends star-free regular languages while being incomparable with regular languages.
conclusion: The logic provides a decidable yet highly expressive formalism for biomedical knowledge, with completeness relative to monadic Presburger validity, but not plain Presburger arithmetic.

title: Towards Scalable Fuzzy Psi Via Efficient Fuzzy Matching
authors: Meng Hao, Xinpeng Yang, Hanxiao Chen, Tianwei Zhang, Haiyang Xue, Guomin Yang, Hongwei Li, Robert H. Deng
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11526v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present scalable fuzzy PSI protocols for general [MATH] distance, supporting both low- and high-dimensional sets. The core technique is two efficient fuzzy matching protocols. The first is built from a role-reversed oblivious PRF (OPRF) and realizes [MATH] overhead, compared to [MATH] in previous works. The second leverages customized oblivious transfer (OT) with [MATH] overhead, where [MATH] is the bit length of inputs, which is particularly suitable for short inputs. With these new techniques, we further propose a new dual-layer hashing framework for fuzzy PSI over low-dimensional sets, instantiated with our OT-based fuzzy matching and enhanced with a domain reduction optimization. The protocols achieve an overhead linear with [MATH], without the [MATH] or [MATH] factors present in prior works. {For high-dimensional sets, we construct fuzzy PSI protocols based on our OPRF- and OT-based fuzzy matching, which achieve an asymptotic overhead linear with [MATH], and [MATH] but rely on the strong globally disjoint assumption.} Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our protocols achieve up to a [MATH] speedup in running time and a [MATH] reduction in communication cost compared to van Baarsen and Pu~(ASIACRYPT'25), and achieve up to a [MATH] speedup in running time and up to a [MATH] reduction in communication cost compared to Piske et al.~(CCS'25).
tldr: This paper presents scalable fuzzy private set intersection (PSI) protocols using efficient fuzzy matching techniques, focusing on cryptographic efficiency rather than quantum information.
motivation: The paper aims to improve the efficiency of fuzzy PSI protocols, which are used for secure matching of similar data without revealing exact values, addressing limitations in prior works.
method: The authors introduce two fuzzy matching protocols: one based on role-reversed oblivious PRF (OPRF) and another using customized oblivious transfer (OT), and propose a dual-layer hashing framework for low-dimensional sets.
result: The protocols achieve linear overhead in input size, eliminating factors present in prior works, and demonstrate significant speedups and communication reductions compared to recent protocols.
conclusion: The proposed fuzzy PSI protocols offer scalable and efficient solutions for secure fuzzy matching, with potential applications in privacy-preserving data analysis.

title: Fingerprinting Text-to-Image Diffusion Models Via Collapsed Generation
authors: Yuanmin Huang, Chen Chen, Geng Hong, Xiaoyu You, Hui Xue, Zhenxing Qian, Mi Zhang, Min Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proprietary text-to-image diffusion models are increasingly distributed as hosted services and downloadable checkpoints, making their intellectual property (IP) protection an increasingly critical concern when model leakage, copying, or unauthorized fine-tuning is disputed. In this work, we present a non-invasive model fingerprinting framework based on , a phenomenon where certain input conditions produce highly consistent images across multiple stochastic seeds. We show that collapsed generation is an intrinsic, model-dependent property of the learned generation process. These collapse-prone conditions therefore expose model-specific behavioral signatures, enabling reliable ownership verification without embedding invasive watermarks. After preparing conditions on the source model, the framework verifies a suspect model under two access settings: (1) white-box pipeline access, where optimized continuous embeddings can be injected into the generation process, and (2) black-box API-only access, where natural language prompts are queried through the service interface. In both cases, ownership evidence is measured by whether the suspect model reproduces the source model's collapse behavior across stochastic samplings. Extensive experiments across UNet- and transformer-based diffusion models show that collapsed generation fingerprints can distinguish different source models with low confusion. These fingerprints remain verifiable in fine-tuned derivatives and under common and adaptive model- or query-level obfuscations, while requiring only a modest verification query budget. Together, these results establish collapsed generation as a reliable intrinsic evidence source for non-invasive diffusion model ownership verification.
tldr: This paper proposes a non-invasive fingerprinting method for text-to-image diffusion models based on collapsed generation, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper addresses intellectual property protection for proprietary text-to-image diffusion models, which is a concern in machine learning and cybersecurity, not in quantum information science.
method: The method identifies input conditions that cause collapsed generation (consistent outputs across seeds) and uses these as fingerprints to verify model ownership under white-box and black-box access.
result: Experiments show that collapsed generation fingerprints can distinguish different diffusion models with low confusion and remain robust to fine-tuning and obfuscations.
conclusion: Collapsed generation provides a reliable intrinsic evidence source for non-invasive diffusion model ownership verification, but it is outside the scope of the user's research interests.

title: Rank-Two Frobenius-Linearized Normal Forms And Orthoderivative Dual Coordinates In Quadratic Apn Maps
authors: Jingchuan Ma, Yanhua Liu, Qiaoyun Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11939v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify binary-linear two-term Frobenius-linearized operators [MATH] on [MATH], where [MATH] is a finite extension of [MATH] and [MATH] is a fixed nontrivial Frobenius automorphism of [MATH] with fixed field [MATH]. Under a coefficient-rank and binary-kernel condition, if [MATH] and [MATH] both have [MATH]-rank two and [MATH] has a one-dimensional kernel over [MATH], then invertible [MATH]-linear input and output changes reduce [MATH], for this fixed [MATH], to the canonical model [MATH]. The proof constructs the coordinate frames from the two coefficient-kernel directions and the binary kernel. In these coordinates, the first dual output row is exactly the unique nonzero trace-adjoint normal, with an exact [MATH]-valued normalization. For pure [MATH]-quadratic almost perfect nonlinear maps, this identifies the orthoderivative by [MATH]; in odd extension degree it also yields permutation behavior and a bijection from the projective plane to its dual. The triprojective construction of Gologlu and Kolsch and the cubic norm-twist construction of Li, Zhou, Li, and Qu provide two realizations arising from different algebraic constructions. The triprojective case further admits a determinant factorization and a complete dual frame, whereas the norm-twist realization shows that the pure-map consequences do not follow from the operator theorem alone. A natural Gold representation has coefficient-rank pair [MATH], delimiting the rank-two subclass. The normal form also supplies exact extension-field labels for known component-radical and Walsh-support relations.
tldr: This paper classifies binary-linear two-term Frobenius-linearized operators and derives canonical normal forms for quadratic APN maps, focusing on algebraic structures rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The research interests focus on quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems; this paper is purely in finite field theory and cryptography, with no connection to those areas.
method: The authors use algebraic classification of Frobenius-linearized operators under coefficient-rank and kernel conditions, constructing coordinate frames and normal forms.
result: They obtain canonical models for rank-two operators and identify orthoderivative dual coordinates for quadratic APN maps, with applications to permutation behavior and projective plane bijections.
conclusion: The work is a contribution to pure mathematics/cryptography, not aligned with the user's research directions.

title: Structural Morphisms For Nested Conditions - Full Version
authors: Andrea Corradini Arend Rensink
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nested conditions are used, among other things, as a graphical way to express first order formulas ruling the applicability of a graph transformation rule to a given match. In this paper, we first introduce several operators on conditions mimicking logical connectives. Next we propose an original notion of structural morphism among nested conditions, and we identify circumstances under which morphisms are consistent with the entailment of the corresponding conditions. Finally we frame the results in a categorical context, proving functoriality and universality properties of the various operations.
tldr: This paper introduces structural morphisms for nested conditions in graph transformation, with categorical properties, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: Nested conditions are used to express first-order formulas for graph transformation rules, and the authors aim to define morphisms that are consistent with entailment.
method: The paper defines operators on nested conditions mimicking logical connectives, proposes a notion of structural morphism, and proves functoriality and universality in a categorical framework.
result: The authors identify conditions under which structural morphisms are consistent with entailment and prove categorical properties of the operations.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of graph transformation and nested conditions, but has no connection to the user's research interests.

title: Diffuse To Compress: Leveraging Diffusion LMs For Lossless Compression
authors: Paolo Ferragina Angelo Nardone
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11249v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the problem of lossless text compression, motivated by the rapid growth in the collection and storage of digital textual data - including plain text, source code, and structured formats such as XML - and by recent advances in neural language model-based compression. In particular, recent LLM-based approaches, whether built on symbol-ranking pipelines or paired with a statistical compressor, have demonstrated compression ratios significantly superior to general-purpose compressors such as zstd, gzip, or bzip on text and code. However, these neural approaches suffer from severe throughput limitations, making them not yet practically usable. For the first time in the context of lossless neural text compression, we introduce Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) as an alternative inference paradigm to autoregressive LLM-based approaches. We argue that replacing autoregressive LLMs with DLMs within the same compression framework could overcome the throughput bottleneck caused by their one-symbol-per-step limitation. However, achieving these improvements requires addressing algorithmic challenges introduced by applying DLMs to lossless compression, where the architecture allows the number and positions of symbols encoded at each forward pass to be decided independently. We design efficient and effective strategies to solve these challenges and evaluate them experimentally against LLM-based and general-purpose compressors on enwik8, a well-established textual benchmark. Our results show that the newly proposed DLM-based framework advances the state of the art in lossless text compression. Moreover, as DLMs are still a relatively young paradigm, recent advances toward increasingly capable and efficient models suggest substantial room for further improvements.
tldr: This paper introduces Diffusion Language Models for lossless text compression, achieving state-of-the-art compression ratios but with throughput improvements over autoregressive LLMs.
motivation: The rapid growth of digital text data and the high compression ratios of LLM-based methods motivate the need for practical neural compression, but current LLM approaches suffer from severe throughput limitations.
method: The authors replace autoregressive LLMs with Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) in a lossless compression framework, designing strategies to handle the flexible number and positions of symbols encoded per forward pass.
result: The DLM-based framework advances the state of the art in lossless text compression on enwik8, while addressing throughput bottlenecks.
conclusion: DLMs offer a promising alternative for neural lossless compression, with potential for further improvements as DLM technology advances.

title: A Methodological Approach For Design Of Energy Efficient Urban Logistics Systems
authors: Emilienne Lardy (CGS I3), Mariam Lafkihi (CGS I3), Eric Ballot
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One of the main challenges for the future in logistics lies in energy consumption. France has the ambition to reach net zero carbon emissions by 2050. The most ambitious research work envisioning the solutions to do so is ___Futurs {\'e}nerg{\'e}tiques 2050' (October 2021) by RTE, the company in charge of the French Electricity Transportation Network. The work assesses multiple scenarios involving various energy mixes (wind, solar, nuclear etc.). It concludes that the net carbon neutrality in 2050 can only be made possible through sobriety, despite mobility switch to electricity (i.e. at least a 40% decrease final energy consumption, plummeting from 1600 TWh to 930 TWh in 2050). In the logistics field, vast progress has been made to lower the energy intensity of road freight transport. Some promising solutions and technologies have been introduced, namely the improvement of vehicle performances, the alternatives fuels, as well as the parallel evolution of physical and digital infrastructures. It resulted in a cut from 0.077 tonne of oil equivalent per thousand tonne-km in 1992 to 0.057 in 2012 (Llorca and Jamasb, 2017). But the simultaneous soar in freight flows quantity and traffic prevented a global decrease in energy consumption. This challenge is stepped up in urban logistics, as it involves managing -in already congested cities- supply channels and small vehicles that are amplifying, multiplying, and becoming more and more intricate. It seems that all the solutions and technologies that have been introduced are necessary, but insufficient, to meet the expectations in terms of energy sobriety. Significant gains will come from a radical shift in logistics shared infrastructure and from innovative organizations. In this vein, CargoCap (Stein and Schoesser, 2003) and other projects are exploring new infrastructures potential while horizontal collaborative transport as a new organization of freight systems has been largely studied and its effectiveness and efficiency has been proven in recent literature (Pan et al., 2019). In this work we will focus on the energy effectiveness of a new freight dedicated infrastructure. This work assesses the potential a large scale cooperative dedicated system, involving shared infrastructure, for the distribution of freight in the city. This is conceived as an alternative to scattered road haulage, in order to significantly cut down energy consumption. With the goal of energy sobriety, we set the twofold objective of modelling the energy consumption of such a dedicated freight supply system, and of drawing conclusions regarding the best practices by means of an impact assessment of the main design parameters. A distribution system's energy demand strongly depends on specific choices of implementation, which can involve putting back on the agenda some discontinued practices, as well as taking advantage of new technologies and innovative processes. Keeping that in mind, our methodology is devised to comprehensively assess all the available implementation choices, both in technology and in layout. The method consists in taking a step back to fundamental energy theorems, which parameters can be set to stand for any scenario of interest. The model includes transportation modes characteristics (e.g. aerodynamics, rolling resistance etc.), as well as kinetics repercussions of delivery management, handling, and infrastructure accessibility (e.g. driving cycles, congestion etc.). For our purposes of generality, but not limited to, the urban layout and the main routing steps are simplified as a general dense area accessed via a ring road. It is applied to the specific case of Paris, benefiting from previous studies and surveys, as well as government approved open data, quantifying all aspects of freight supply. As far as limits are concerned, it can be put forward that the model is overly simplified and blind on indirect energy consumption which is considerable in overall energy demand. Our work precisely spots out the most impactful parameters, and the high potential axis for refinement, factoring uncertainty. It also specifies where direct and indirect energy drives align, and, on the contrary, a judicious compromise should be investigated. These findings give the necessary tools to further the research into a refined and expanded model, a methodology and insights for urban freight distribution applied here in large cities.
tldr: This paper proposes a methodology for modeling energy consumption of a dedicated urban freight distribution system, applied to Paris, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper addresses the challenge of reducing energy consumption in urban logistics to meet France's net-zero carbon goals, focusing on a shared infrastructure alternative to scattered road haulage.
method: The authors develop a model based on fundamental energy theorems, incorporating transportation mode characteristics and delivery management factors, and apply it to a simplified urban layout (ring road) for Paris using open data.
result: The model identifies the most impactful design parameters for energy consumption and highlights where direct and indirect energy drives align or require compromise.
conclusion: The findings provide a methodology and insights for refining urban freight distribution systems, but the model is simplified and needs expansion to account for indirect energy consumption.

title: Dueling Deep Q-Learning For Intrusion Detection
authors: Logan Luna (georgia Institute Of Technology), Matthew P. Berkowitz (embry-Riddle Aeronautical University), Laxima Niure Kandel (embry-Riddle Aeronautical University), Sirio Jansen-S'anchez
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intrusion detection systems (IDS) and automated systems for detecting and reporting cyber threats, are commonly handled via supervised machine learning methods. Though effective, these models struggle to effectively adapt to new attack types. This study proposes a novel approach by employing a reward-based, dueling Q-learning model for IDS, achieving an average accuracy of 99.68% across multiple attack classes. The proposed model has a dueling network architecture which separates its predictions into value and advantage streams. This has the benefit of improving learning efficiency and stability. The model was trained on the CIC-IDS2018, a benchmark dataset based on real-world intrusion detection scenarios, having multiple attack classes such as DDoS, botnets, and brute-force attacks. Furthermore, Explainable AI (XAI), specifically SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), was also integrated into the training and evaluation process to provide interpretability into the model's predictions.
tldr: This paper applies dueling deep Q-learning with SHAP explainability to intrusion detection, achieving high accuracy on the CIC-IDS2018 dataset.
motivation: Intrusion detection systems using supervised learning struggle to adapt to new attack types, motivating a reinforcement learning approach.
method: The authors employ a dueling Q-learning architecture that separates value and advantage streams, and integrate SHAP for interpretability.
result: The model achieves an average accuracy of 99.68% across multiple attack classes on the CIC-IDS2018 benchmark.
conclusion: The proposed reinforcement learning approach shows promise for adaptive intrusion detection, with explainability aiding trust.

title: Unlocking CCUS-Ready Coal Power Investments: A Spatial Real Options Approach
authors: Yun-Long Zhang, Jia-Ning Kang, Lan-Cui Liu, Yi-Zhuo Ji, Song Peng, Yi-Ming Wei
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: New coal-fired capacity may still be needed in some economies to support energy security, yet tightening carbon constraints increasingly threaten its long-term investment viability. Designing new plants to be Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (CCUS)-ready is therefore critical, but existing investment studies largely neglect the spatial factors that shape CCUS investment viability. In this study, we propose a Spatial Real Options (SRO) framework that couples national-scale siting screening with site-level real-options valuation. A national inventory of technically feasible sites across China (n = 194,027) is linked to a real-options model that incorporates temporal uncertainty together with province-specific conditions, CO2 transport distance, and alternative policy instruments. Results show that the nationwide investable window for conventional coal closes by the early-to-mid 2040s. CCUS integration materially reshapes project economics, but outcomes differ substantially across storage options and transport distances: oil-reservoir storage remains economically attractive at short distances, whereas saline-aquifer storage requires operational incentives to become competitive. Generation-hour compensation substantially outperforms investment-cost subsidies, indicating that operating costs, rather than upfront capital, constitute the binding constraint. The resulting spatiotemporal maps provide a practical decision-support tool for identifying where and when CCUS-ready coal investments are most attractive under progressive decarbonization.
tldr: This paper develops a spatial real options framework to evaluate CCUS-ready coal power investments in China, focusing on economic viability under carbon constraints.
motivation: New coal capacity may be needed for energy security, but carbon constraints threaten viability; CCUS-ready design is critical, yet spatial factors are often neglected.
method: The authors couple national-scale siting screening with site-level real-options valuation, incorporating temporal uncertainty, province-specific conditions, CO2 transport distance, and policy instruments.
result: The investable window for conventional coal closes by early-to-mid 2040s; CCUS integration reshapes economics, with oil-reservoir storage attractive at short distances and saline-aquifer storage needing incentives; generation-hour compensation outperforms investment subsidies.
conclusion: The spatiotemporal maps provide a decision-support tool for identifying where and when CCUS-ready coal investments are most attractive under decarbonization.

title: Technology Interactions Reshape The Economics Of China's Coal Power Decarbonization
authors: Yun-Long Zhang, Jia-Ning Kang, Xiaoming Kan, Lan-Cui Liu, Zhimin Huang, Song Peng, Biying Yu, Yi-Ming Wei
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decarbonizing existing coal-fired power plants can contribute to near-term climate mitigation, but identifying cost-effective retrofit strategies is complicated by interactions among mitigation technologies. Here we develop an interaction-aware optimization framework that jointly evaluates energy conservation, biomass co-firing, and carbon capture across 1,885 coal-fired power plants in China while accounting for plant heterogeneity and shared biomass and CO2 storage resources. We find that technology interactions alter both mitigation costs and the emission reductions attributable to individual measures, thereby changing cost-optimal technology portfolios and marginal abatement cost curve at the fleet level. Approximately 1.2 Gt CO2 yr-1 can be mitigated at negative marginal cost, while reaching carbon neutrality requires a marginal abatement cost of US$56 t CO2-1. Progressively deeper mitigation shifts the cost-optimal portfolio from energy conservation toward biomass co-firing and ultimately carbon capture, with biomass combined with carbon capture enabling net-negative emissions. Explicitly accounting for interactions among mitigation technologies therefore provides a more consistent basis for evaluating coal-power decarbonization and coordinating retrofit investment, infrastructure development, and climate policy.
tldr: This paper analyzes the economics of decarbonizing China's coal power plants, focusing on technology interactions and cost-optimal portfolios, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The paper aims to identify cost-effective strategies for decarbonizing coal power in China, considering interactions among mitigation technologies.
method: The authors develop an interaction-aware optimization framework that evaluates energy conservation, biomass co-firing, and carbon capture across 1,885 coal plants, accounting for plant heterogeneity and shared resources.
result: They find that technology interactions alter mitigation costs and emission reductions, with about 1.2 Gt CO2/yr mitigable at negative marginal cost and carbon neutrality requiring $56/t CO2.
conclusion: Accounting for technology interactions provides a more consistent basis for evaluating coal-power decarbonization and coordinating investment and policy.

title: Twenty-Five Years Of Air Quality In Bangladesh: Trends, Seasonality, And Spatial Pollution Regimes
authors: Md Rafid Islam, Rafsan Jany, Md. Siyam Bhuiyan, Rafid Bin Zaman, Mohammad Saifuddin, Sabrina Sultana
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Air pollution is one of Bangladesh's most pressing environmental problems, yet few studies have examined it at a national scale over a long time span. To describe trends, seasonality, geographic patterns, and pollution regimes, this study examines 25 years of hourly air quality data (2000-2025), covering over 3.19 million records, eight pollutants, and 103 cities monitored from 2022 onward following expansion from a single Dhaka station. The composite AQI series showed no significant long-term trend, an artifact of this network expansion rather than a real flattening of pollution, since Dhaka's own AQI rose steadily before the network grew. Seasonality was strong and highly significant, as AQI peaked in January (162.26) and fell to its lowest in July (61.47), tracking the dry and monsoon seasons. Geographically, southeastern coastal cities, including Teknaf and Bandarban, consistently recorded the lowest AQI levels. Dhaka remained the most polluted city, and air quality improved progressively with distance from the capital. K-means clustering of city-level AQI trajectories identified four distinct pollution regimes, ranging from cleaner coastal regions to a rapidly deteriorating Dhaka-Narsingdi cluster with an average increase of 1.84 AQI per year. Correlation analysis showed that PM2.5 and PM10 were the dominant contributors to AQI variation, and so combustion-related emissions are the primary target for air quality management and policy intervention.
tldr: This paper analyzes 25 years of air quality data in Bangladesh, identifying trends, seasonality, and spatial pollution regimes.
motivation: Air pollution is a pressing issue in Bangladesh, but long-term national-scale studies are lacking.
method: The study uses 25 years of hourly air quality data (2000-2025) from 103 cities, applying statistical trend analysis, seasonality decomposition, K-means clustering, and correlation analysis.
result: No significant long-term trend in composite AQI due to network expansion, but strong seasonality with peaks in January and lows in July; Dhaka is most polluted, and four distinct pollution regimes were identified.
conclusion: PM2.5 and PM10 are dominant contributors, indicating combustion-related emissions as primary targets for policy.

title: A Gas-Driven Algorithm For Variants Of The Moving Sofa Problem
authors: Xingyi He
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11206v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a numerical algorithm based on the idea of dynamical systems for solving the moving sofa problem. By introducing a physical model driven by gas pressure, we transform the geometric optimization problem into a dynamical system. Numerical experiments show that the method effectively approximates the known Gerver's sofa result, and provides numerical estimates of the possible maximum area for corridors with different angles. In particular, we observe an intersection of the two motion patterns at [MATH], where the locally maximal sofa area is [MATH], and the dominant pattern switches on either side of this critical angle.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical algorithm based on gas pressure dynamics to solve the moving sofa problem, a geometric optimization problem unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The moving sofa problem is a classic geometric optimization challenge; the authors aim to provide a numerical method to approximate the maximum area of a sofa that can navigate a corridor.
method: The method introduces a physical model driven by gas pressure, transforming the geometric optimization into a dynamical system, and then simulates the system to find locally maximal sofa areas.
result: The algorithm effectively approximates Gerver's known sofa result and provides numerical estimates for corridors with different angles, observing a switch in dominant motion patterns at a critical angle.
conclusion: The paper demonstrates a novel numerical approach to the moving sofa problem, but it has no connection to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Marden's Theorem, Symmetric Parametrizations, And Triangles Circumscribed About Central Conics
authors: Mohammad Hassan Murad
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using a generalized Chapple--Euler relation, we first prove that a central conic with foci [MATH] forms a [MATH]-Poncelet pair with the unit circle if and only if its major axis has length [MATH]. This characterization applies uniformly to both elliptic and hyperbolic cases. Our main result shows that Marden's theorem yields a symmetric parametrization of every such Poncelet family. If [MATH] are the vertices of a circumscribed triangle, then their elementary symmetric functions admit explicit formulas in terms of the foci [MATH] and a unimodular parameter [MATH]. As a consequence, the classical degree-three Blaschke-product equation arises directly from Marden's theorem and remains valid without requiring the foci to lie inside the unit disk. The parametrization provides a unified framework for deriving geometric invariants of families of circumscribed triangles. We obtain invariants related to orthocenters and side lengths, and give a short proof of the classical theorem which states that the circumcircle of a triangle formed by three tangents to a parabola passes through the focus. Finally, we establish a higher-degree symmetric parametrization for partial fractions with finite numbers of poles, leading to generalized M\"obius-product equations. The associated residues satisfy a partition-of-unity identity extending the classical Marden weights, thereby placing Marden's theorem within a broader residue-theoretic framework and suggesting possible higher-degree analogues in Poncelet geometry.
tldr: This paper proves a symmetric parametrization of Poncelet triangles circumscribed about central conics using Marden's theorem, with applications to geometric invariants and higher-degree analogues.
motivation: The paper aims to unify and extend classical results in Poncelet geometry and Marden's theorem, providing a general framework for circumscribed triangles and partial fractions.
method: The author uses a generalized Chapple-Euler relation and Marden's theorem to derive symmetric parametrizations, and extends to higher-degree partial fractions with generalized Möbius-product equations.
result: The main results include a characterization of central conics forming Poncelet pairs with the unit circle, explicit formulas for symmetric functions of triangle vertices, and a partition-of-unity identity for residues.
conclusion: The work places Marden's theorem in a broader residue-theoretic framework, suggesting potential higher-degree analogues in Poncelet geometry.

title: Heavy Ball Gmresr Method For Nonsymmetric Linear Systems
authors: Mei Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11270v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The heavy ball GMRES (HBGMRES) method is one of Krylov subspace methods for linear systems combined with the restarted GMRES and the heavy ball method which is applied in optimization. HBGMRES not only keeps benefit of the restarted GMRES in limiting memory usage and controlling orthogonalization cost, but also is able to cover up the slow convergence problem in the restarted GMRES. Another type of Krylov subspace methods is GMRESR which consists of GCR as the outer algorithm and certain steps of GMRES as an inner method. Compared with HBGMRES, GMRESR gives the approximately optimal solution over the new search vector gained from GMRES and all previously kept search vectors in GCR. Even though GMRESR performs better than HBGMRES, it has slow convergence which is similar to GMRES and the restarted GMRES. Inspired by HBGMRES, we present the heavy ball GMRESR method (HBGMRESR) by using HBGMRES as the inner loop instead of using GMRES to salvage the lost convergence speed while still keeping the benefit of GMRESR that in the sense of a global minimization over some specific part of the Krylov subspace is done. Numerical tests on real data are presented to demonstratee the superiority of the new methods over GMRESR and HBGMRES.
tldr: This paper proposes a new Krylov subspace method (HBGMRESR) for solving nonsymmetric linear systems, combining heavy ball acceleration with GMRESR.
motivation: The restarted GMRES and GMRESR methods suffer from slow convergence for certain problems; the heavy ball method from optimization can accelerate convergence.
method: The authors replace the inner GMRES in GMRESR with HBGMRES, which incorporates a heavy ball momentum term, to create HBGMRESR.
result: Numerical tests on real data show that HBGMRESR outperforms both GMRESR and HBGMRES in terms of convergence speed.
conclusion: HBGMRESR is a promising iterative method for nonsymmetric linear systems, offering improved convergence while retaining the memory benefits of restarted methods.

title: Exact Characterisation Of Maximum-angle Conditions For Spherical Finite Element Meshes
authors: Hiroki Ishizaka
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Maximum-angle conditions are standard finite-element mesh hypotheses that permit anisotropic triangles excluded by minimum-angle or shape-regularity assumptions. For exact spherical triangles, however, the angles of the chordal affine core and the intrinsic spherical angles need not coincide, while radial geometry introduces curvature-scale distortion. We give an algebraic characterisation of the intrinsic spherical maximum-angle condition through a dimensionless quantity computed from the three vertex vectors. A uniform positive lower bound on this quantity is equivalent to a uniform spherical maximum-angle bound and requires neither spherical-angle nor spherical-area evaluation. We identify the support-plane geometry linking the chordal circumradius to radial distortion and derive sharp comparisons between the intrinsic spherical and chordal semi-regularity parameters. In particular, a locality-independent comparison holds with sharp constant [MATH] and a characterised equality case. An area-based parameter is shown to be smaller than the spherical semi-regularity parameter, with sharp constant one in the local flat limit. For spherical finite-element meshes, the vertex criterion implies uniform chordal semi-regularity with an explicit constant, while relative refinement makes the radial-distortion factors converge uniformly to one. Thus, the intrinsic criterion, together with relative refinement, provides the geometric controls used in anisotropic finite-element analysis without imposing a minimum-angle or shape-regularity condition.

motivation: The paper addresses the need for mesh quality criteria in finite element analysis on spherical domains, where traditional angle conditions are complicated by curvature.
method: The authors derive a dimensionless quantity from vertex vectors that characterizes the intrinsic spherical maximum-angle condition, and compare it with chordal semi-regularity parameters.
result: They establish sharp comparisons between spherical and chordal parameters, and show that the vertex criterion implies uniform chordal semi-regularity with explicit constants.
conclusion: The intrinsic criterion, combined with relative refinement, provides geometric controls for anisotropic finite element analysis without imposing minimum-angle or shape-regularity conditions.
