title: Predict-then-Optimize Framework For Public Transport Line Redesign Under Fluctuating Traffic Conditions
authors: Zihao Guo, Andrea Araldo, Faycal Touzout, Mounim El-Yacoubi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Public Transport (PT) lines are traditionally designed to optimize performance under nominal traffic conditions. In practice, operating conditions frequently deviate from nominal ones, leading to substantial performance deterioration. Existing adaptation mechanisms typically rely on reactive interventions, such as stop-skipping, which are insufficient under large or recurrent traffic fluctuations. In such contexts, incremental adjustments may not suffice. This paper evaluates the potential of deeper structural redesigns to preserve performance. We propose a method to proactively redesign appropriate parts of PT networks under high traffic fluctuations that would otherwise deteriorate operator and user performance. We adopt a predict-then-optimize paradigm in which PT lines are reconfigured based on traffic forecasts using the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III). To ensure operational feasibility and avoid excessive structural changes, we enforce high Jaccard edge overlap between the original and redesigned networks. To assess prediction inaccuracies, we construct a statistical model of errors from a well-established deep learning predictor, the Diffusion Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network, trained on real-world data. Computational results on Mandl's benchmark and the large-scale Beijing network show that controlled PT line redesign yields substantial user-centric performance gains and operational cost reductions under high traffic fluctuations while limiting topological changes. On the Beijing network under high variability, average travel time improves by up to 25.8% while preserving over 85% line overlap. Unlike stop-skipping baselines, which break connectivity for many OD pairs, our redesign preserves full OD connectivity. These results support a shift from static planning toward continuous and adaptive PT network design.
tldr: This paper proposes a predict-then-optimize framework using NSGA-III to redesign public transport lines under fluctuating traffic conditions, showing performance gains on benchmark networks.
motivation: Public transport lines are designed for nominal conditions and degrade under traffic fluctuations; reactive measures like stop-skipping are insufficient for large fluctuations.
method: The method uses traffic forecasts from a deep learning model (DCRNN) to drive NSGA-III optimization for line redesign, enforcing high Jaccard overlap to limit structural changes.
result: On the Beijing network, average travel time improves by up to 25.8% while preserving over 85% line overlap, and full OD connectivity is maintained unlike stop-skipping baselines.
conclusion: The results support a shift from static planning to continuous adaptive PT network design to handle traffic variability.

title: Linear-cost Polyharmonic Spline Interpolation Of Arbitrary Degree
authors: Michael O'neil Christopher J. Geoga
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a simple and performant approach for rapidly and accurately performing polyharmonic spline (PHS) interpolation using a combination of the fast multipole method (FMM) from computational electrostatics and the Vecchia approximation from the Gaussian process and sparse approximate inverse literatures. Using basic properties about Hadamard products and low-rank matrices, we demonstrate that an FMM with two kernels, the logarithmic and distance kernels, results in fast PHS interpolation for all orders. Furthermore, we demonstrate the exceptional performance of sparse inverse approximation methods with the Mat\'ern covariance model for preconditioning. Combined with careful management of disallowed subspaces, we describe a procedure for obtaining prediction weights using preconditioned conjugate gradient that converges in less than [MATH] iterations, even for problem sizes with over one million points. As a result, thin-plate spline interpolation---a particularly popular method that does not require parameter tuning---that matches the fully dense [MATH] computation in accuracy can be done at the cost of approximately [MATH] FMMs. A high-performance software library for odd-order PHS interpolation in two dimensions is made available as a companion to this work.

motivation: The authors aim to accelerate polyharmonic spline interpolation, which is computationally expensive for large datasets, by leveraging fast multipole methods and sparse approximations.

conclusion: The proposed approach enables fast and accurate polyharmonic spline interpolation, with a software library provided for practical use.

title: Nonlinear Stability, Resonances, And Singular Reduction In The Unequal-Mass Equilateral Restricted Four-Body Problem
authors: Martha \'alvarez-Ram\'irez J. Alejandro Zepeda-Ram\'irez
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the nonlinear stability of the elliptic equilibrium points [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH] in the planar equilateral restricted four-body problem with unequal primary masses. title: Contour Hankel Dynamics And Indicator Fields For The Riemann $\Xi$-function
authors: Zhiliang Deng, Xiaomei Yang, Huazhong L\"u
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a moving-contour Hankel framework for encoding local zero configurations of the Riemann [MATH]-function. Weighted contour integrals of the logarithmic derivative [MATH], expressed in a holomorphic coordinate associated with the contour, are identified with the power moments of a finite atomic measure supported at the coordinate images of the enclosed zeros. This representation yields exact zero-free and rank criteria and, for conjugation-compatible contour-coordinate pairs, an inertia formula: once the matrix order is at least the number of distinct coordinate nodes, the negative index equals the number of distinct nonreal conjugate pairs. Consequently, the Riemann hypothesis admits a local finite-dimensional Hankel-positivity formulation, although establishing this positivity independently of the zero set remains unresolved. As the contour moves, the Hankel matrix evolves by a continuous congruence flow between zero crossings and undergoes finite-rank jumps at crossing events. An isolated zero produces a signed rank-one jump, whereas a nonreal conjugate pair produces a rank-two indefinite event in a real-axis circular scan that meets the pair. Removing the continuous coordinate drift yields a piecewise-constant matrix process from which crossing coordinates, multiplicities, and zero locations can be recovered. Numerical experiments validate the contour quadrature, indicator fields, continuous flow, crossing signatures, and recovery procedure.

motivation: The paper aims to provide a new mathematical formulation for the Riemann hypothesis using contour integrals and Hankel matrices.
method: It introduces moving-contour Hankel dynamics, representing zero configurations via power moments of atomic measures, and derives inertia formulas and flow equations.
result: It yields exact zero-free criteria and a local finite-dimensional Hankel-positivity formulation of the Riemann hypothesis, with numerical validation.
conclusion: The work is purely mathematical, focusing on analytic number theory, and does not relate to the user's research interests.

title: An Interface Green's Function Framework For Complete Discrete $W^{1,\infty}$ Analysis Of Discontinuous Galerkin Methods
authors: Weifeng Qiu Haitao Leng
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pointwise error analysis of discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods has received considerable attention during the past two decades. Existing analyses establish optimal error estimates in the [MATH] norm and the broken [MATH] seminorm for several DG methods. However, since the broken [MATH] seminorm does not control discontinuities across mesh interfaces, a complete discrete [MATH] theory for discontinuous approximations has remained unavailable. title: Whirliness Beyond Amenability

abstract: ArXiv:2608.11662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a non-atomic standard probability space [MATH], we exhibit examples of non-amenable closed topological subgroups of [MATH] whose natural near-action on [MATH] is whirly. title: A Statistical Theory Of Graph Regularization For Rna Velocity Near Developmental Bifurcations
authors: Shiruo Wang Lingqi Meng
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graph-based regularization is widely used to stabilize noisy RNA-velocity estimates by encouraging transcriptionally similar cells to share similar velocity vectors. Near developmental bifurcations, however, proximity-based graphs may connect cells from distinct daughter lineages, reducing estimation variance at the cost of attenuating biologically meaningful lineage-specific dynamics. We formulate graph-regularized RNA velocity as a statistical estimation problem on a potentially misspecified cell-state graph and develop a theoretical framework for analyzing this trade-off. We derive an exact graph-spectral bias--variance decomposition that characterizes how Laplacian regularization suppresses estimation noise while introducing systematic smoothing bias. To quantify lineage preservation, we introduce a branch-sensitive risk that separates within-lineage denoising from cross-lineage information leakage. We further show that persistent cross-branch connectivity can induce nonvanishing branch bias, implying that standard proximity-graph regularization may remain asymptotically inconsistent near developmental bifurcations. These results provide a mathematical foundation for understanding both the statistical benefits and the geometric limitations of graph regularization for RNA-velocity estimation.
tldr: This paper develops a statistical theory for graph regularization in RNA velocity estimation, focusing on bias-variance trade-offs near developmental bifurcations.
motivation: Graph-based regularization is used to stabilize noisy RNA-velocity estimates, but near bifurcations it may attenuate lineage-specific dynamics. The authors aim to understand this trade-off theoretically.
method: They formulate graph-regularized RNA velocity as a statistical estimation problem on a misspecified graph, derive an exact graph-spectral bias-variance decomposition, and introduce a branch-sensitive risk to quantify lineage preservation.
result: They show that persistent cross-branch connectivity can cause nonvanishing branch bias, implying standard proximity-graph regularization may be asymptotically inconsistent near bifurcations.
conclusion: The work provides a mathematical foundation for understanding the statistical benefits and geometric limitations of graph regularization for RNA-velocity estimation.

title: A Wolfe-Type Spectral Conjugate Gradient Method For Nonsmooth Convex Optimization Problems
authors: Gourav Kumar Jauny
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a Wolfe-type spectral conjugate gradient method for nonsmooth convex optimization, built on the Moreau-Yosida regularization of the objective function. The method combines a safeguarded spectral parameter with a Dai-Kou-type conjugate parameter, and uses a Wolfe-type line search compatible with the inexact gradients that the regularization produces. We establish global convergence of the method, together with an R-linear convergence rate under an additional strong-convexity assumption. The method is evaluated on standard nonsmooth optimization benchmarks and on large-scale problems, and compared against several existing conjugate gradient and bundle-type methods. The results show that the proposed method performs competitively overall, matching or outperforming existing methods on most problems tested, while a few specific limitations of the current implementation are also identified and discussed.

motivation: The paper aims to improve optimization methods for nonsmooth convex problems, which is a classical optimization topic.
method: It combines a safeguarded spectral parameter with a Dai-Kou-type conjugate parameter and uses a Wolfe-type line search compatible with inexact gradients from Moreau-Yosida regularization.

title: Area-Normalized Pentagram Map Dynamics: Spectral Flattening And Elliptic Asymptotics

abstract: ArXiv:2608.11781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The pentagram map sends a polygon to the intersections of consecutive short diagonals. Consequently, we recover Schwartz's long-and-thin result for strictly convex non-projectively-regular pentagons, prove a line-or-ellipse dichotomy for convex hexagons under explicit nondegeneracy assumptions, and establish flattening for strictly convex non-projectively-regular Poncelet polygons.

conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive spectral framework for the pentagram map, but it has no connection to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Induction And The Rule Of Succession Through A Possibilistic Inferential Model Lens
authors: Ryan Martin, Shih-Ni Prim, Jonathan P. Williams
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Induction is the process by which empirical evidence is transformed to knowledge. Hume famously argued---and Popper and others agree---that there can be no logical justification for induction. A weaker form of induction, due to Bayes, expresses the aforementioned knowledge in terms of probabilities, and we review some well-known and not-so-well-known criticisms of the Bayesian solution. We then investigate the relatively new possibilistic inferential model (IM) framework, showing that, in addition to the IM's strong, statistical reliability guarantees that it uniquely enjoys, it is safe from those criticisms that damage the Bayesian foundations. For illustration, we reconsider the classical sunrise problem and compare our proposed solution with Laplace's famous rule of succession.

motivation: The paper addresses philosophical and statistical issues with Bayesian induction, proposing a possibilistic alternative.
method: It reviews criticisms of Bayesian inference and applies the possibilistic inferential model (IM) framework to the sunrise problem.
result: The IM approach avoids certain criticisms and provides a solution to the sunrise problem.
conclusion: The possibilistic IM framework offers a robust alternative to Bayesian induction.

Positivity is preserved for nonnegative data without a diagonal-dominance condition and without any CFL-type relation between [MATH] and [MATH].
tldr: This paper presents a positivity-preserving numerical scheme for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations with oblique Robin boundary conditions, using a probabilistic interpretation via reflected Feynman-Kac identities.
motivation: The paper addresses the challenge of constructing positivity-preserving schemes for degenerate HJB equations with oblique Robin boundary conditions, which is important for applications in control theory and finance.
method: The method constructs a finite difference scheme based on a one-step reflected Feynman-Kac identity, using Rademacher vectors to generate weak-Euler branches and mirroring exterior branches to handle boundary conditions.
result: The scheme preserves positivity for nonnegative data without diagonal-dominance or CFL conditions, and yields a sparse nonsingular M-matrix system for linear Robin data.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a robust numerical method for HJB equations with oblique Robin boundary conditions, with theoretical guarantees on positivity and stability.

title: Subregular Affine Cells And The Level $-1$ Vertex Algebra Of Type $d$
authors: Sihai Jin
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the Shan--Yan--Zhao affine left-cell conjecture for the simple affine vertex algebras [MATH], [MATH]. The distinguished vacuum block has exactly [MATH] simple objects, indexed by the subregular affine left cell containing [MATH]. Two finite-dimensional ingredients enter the proof. A primitive-ideal inclusion shows that the predicted non-vacuum modules descend to the relevant quotient, while a separate exhaustion argument rules out further highest weights. It follows that the Grothendieck group is the [MATH] specialization of the corresponding dual affine left-cell module. The same identification yields uniform character formulas in terms of subregular inverse Kazhdan--Lusztig coefficients.
tldr: This paper proves a conjecture about affine left cells and vertex algebras of type D, which is a topic in representation theory and vertex algebras, not related to the user's research interests.
motivation: The paper aims to prove the Shan-Yan-Zhao affine left-cell conjecture for certain simple affine vertex algebras, contributing to the understanding of their structure.
method: The proof uses primitive-ideal inclusions and an exhaustion argument to show that the predicted modules descend to the quotient and rule out further highest weights.
result: The paper establishes the conjecture, identifies the Grothendieck group as a specialization of a dual affine left-cell module, and provides character formulas using subregular inverse Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients.
conclusion: The work resolves a conjecture in representation theory, but it is outside the scope of the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Adaptive Bregman Proximal Stochastic Gradient With A Stabilized Barzilai--Borwein Step Size
authors: Chenhan Jin, Shengze Xu, Binghui Xie, Kaiwen Zhou, Fan Jia, James Cheng, Tieyong Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bregman proximal stochastic gradient (BPSG) methods bring variance-reduced composite optimization to objectives whose geometry is poorly captured by Euclidean smoothness. Their performance, however, remains sensitive to the step size: raw stochastic curvature estimates can fluctuate sharply, whereas line searches add repeated proximal evaluations. We introduce Ada-BPSG, a line-search-free BPSG method that couples the SAGA gradient table with a stabilized Barzilai--Borwein (BB) candidate. A mediant aggregates incremental secant information so that nearly singular local ratios receive little weight, and an explicit safeguard translates the resulting curvature estimate into the bounded step-size sequence required for convergence. This design yields a direct analytical chain from relative smoothness and component-wise variance control to convergence in finite-dimensional normed spaces. We prove an [MATH] ergodic rate for convex objectives, a restarted linear rate under relative quadratic growth, and an [MATH] bound for a Bregman proximal residual in the nonconvex setting. On logistic regression and sparse nonnegative matrix factorization, Ada-BPSG combines low objective values with substantially less sensitivity to the initial step size than standard variance-reduced baselines, while avoiding line search.
tldr: This paper introduces a line-search-free Bregman proximal stochastic gradient method with a stabilized Barzilai-Borwein step size for composite optimization.
motivation: The paper addresses the sensitivity of Bregman proximal stochastic gradient methods to step size selection, which can be unstable due to fluctuating curvature estimates or expensive line searches.
method: The proposed Ada-BPSG method combines the SAGA gradient table with a stabilized Barzilai-Borwein step size, using a mediant to aggregate secant information and a safeguard to ensure bounded step sizes, enabling convergence analysis.
result: The method achieves an ergodic rate for convex objectives, a restarted linear rate under relative quadratic growth, and a bound for a Bregman proximal residual in the nonconvex setting, with improved robustness to initial step size on logistic regression and sparse NMF.
conclusion: Ada-BPSG provides a practical, line-search-free alternative for variance-reduced composite optimization, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Benchmarking Cyberattack Detection In Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure With Benign User Updates
authors: Hannan Chen, Roshni Anna Jacob, Jie Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cyberattack detection in electric vehicle charging infrastructure is complicated by legitimate post-activation revisions to requested energy and departure time. Charging manipulation attacks can exploit the same interface and variables; therefore, detecting a request change alone does not establish malicious intent. This paper develops a leakage-controlled session-level benchmark that preserves the ordered inputs of real Adaptive Charging Network (ACN) sessions and models legitimate revisions as normal behavior. A fixed pool keeps each generated attack in its source session's split and contains six physically motivated attacks and their coordinated variants. We compare 22 profile-only, transition-aware, and context-stratified model families under common source-grouped folds, attack data, and operating constraints. The proposed Dual-Branch Masked-Autoencoder (Masked-AE) Transition Boost model evaluates whether the current request is normal and whether its producing transition resembles an observed benign update. Its state branch combines masked reconstruction with a radial-basis-function one-class support boundary, while its transition branch combines masked reconstruction with shrinkage covariance distance. Source-grouped five-fold cross-validation selects complete configurations under explicit overall-normal and benign-update acceptance constraints; disjoint normal data then calibrate the final threshold before one test evaluation. The developed dual-branch model provides the strongest robust validation performance while detecting malicious request manipulations without learning to reject legitimate user choices.
tldr: This paper benchmarks cyberattack detection in electric vehicle charging infrastructure, focusing on distinguishing malicious request manipulations from legitimate user updates.
motivation: Cyberattacks on EV charging infrastructure can exploit the same interface as legitimate user revisions, making detection challenging. The authors aim to provide a benchmark and a model that can detect attacks without rejecting benign user choices.
method: They develop a leakage-controlled session-level benchmark using real ACN data, with six physically motivated attack types. They compare 22 model families and propose a Dual-Branch Masked-Autoencoder Transition Boost model that combines masked reconstruction with one-class classification and covariance distance to assess both the current request and its transition.
result: The proposed dual-branch model achieves the strongest robust validation performance in detecting malicious request manipulations while maintaining acceptance of legitimate user updates.
conclusion: The study provides a benchmark and a model that effectively detects cyberattacks in EV charging infrastructure, balancing security and user flexibility.

title: Backdoor Decontamination Dynamics In Llm Agents
authors: Gabriel Huang, Abhay Puri, L\'eo Boisvert, Alexandre Drouin, Perouz Taslakian, Spandana Gella, Christopher Pal
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-weight LLM agents are vulnerable to backdoors installed during fine-tuning, which may be undetectable if the trigger conditions are never met during testing. Assuming defenders do not know the existing trigger, they cannot unlearn it directly. One decontamination strategy is to install a known backdoor (defensive poisoning) then to unlearn it, hoping that the original unknown backdoor is removed as a side effect. However, this procedure has uncertain outcomes: the original backdoor may persist or be erased or rerouted, among other possibilities. We introduce a framework for studying these dynamics in tool-calling agents, decoupling trigger, response, teacher, and fine-tuning method across systematic experiments on AgentDyn. Across 115 experiments, defensive poisoning alone erases around 56% of original backdoors; subsequent decontamination then drives almost all survivors to erasure, confirming that trigger recognition and malicious execution are behaviorally dissociable. Interestingly, our experiments find that malicious backdoors never persist when using different triggers of the same general type as the defensive backdoor when followed by decontamination via unlearning. Co-installing up to four backdoors increases resistance (around 36% erased), yet decontaminating a single known co-resident backdoor collaterally clears 52/60 co-residents (87%). Upon visualizing postdecontamination model internals using J-lens, we confirm that although the decontamination restores benign LLM responses, traces of original trigger awareness persist at intermediate layers.
tldr: This paper studies backdoor decontamination dynamics in LLM agents, focusing on defensive poisoning and unlearning to remove unknown backdoors.
motivation: Open-weight LLM agents are vulnerable to backdoors installed during fine-tuning, which may be undetectable if triggers are never met. Defenders need strategies to remove unknown backdoors without knowing the trigger.
method: The authors introduce a framework to study backdoor decontamination in tool-calling agents, decoupling trigger, response, teacher, and fine-tuning method across 115 experiments on AgentDyn. They use defensive poisoning (installing a known backdoor) followed by unlearning, and analyze model internals with J-lens.
result: Defensive poisoning alone erases about 56% of original backdoors; subsequent decontamination drives almost all survivors to erasure. Co-installing up to four backdoors increases resistance, but decontaminating one known backdoor clears 87% of co-residents. Traces of original trigger awareness persist in intermediate layers.
conclusion: Backdoor decontamination via defensive poisoning and unlearning is effective, but residual trigger awareness remains, suggesting a need for more thorough decontamination methods.

title: An Empirical Study Of Output-to-Input Loops For Black-Box Backdoor Detection In Fine-Tuned Open-Weight LLMs
authors: Mohammad Arif Hossain Md. Nahid Hasan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anyone can upload a fine-tuned large language model (LLM) to a public repository and claim it is safe. A backdoored model behaves normally on ordinary inputs until a hidden trigger fires, and a user with no training data, clean reference weights, or the trigger phrase has no clear way to check the model before using it. We introduce and empirically evaluate self-feeding, a black-box test method that feeds a model's own output back as its next input, so the text drifts away from the starting prompt and toward the data the model was fine-tuned on. We test self-feeding against a repeated same-prompt baseline on six open-weight LLMs (3B-15B parameters), each fine-tuned with backdoors spanning eleven attack categories, using twenty ordinary starting prompts and chains of up to ten steps. Self-feeding finds backdoors in five of six models at 92.0\% pooled precision, while the same-prompt baseline succeeds on only one of 120 prompt-model pairs; chains that begin with a joke request, an arithmetic question, or a coffee recipe all reach a trigger within a few steps. Recall per prompt is low (19.2\%), and we show why it still adds up to much higher detection at the model level once several starting prompts are used. We also report where the method falls short: one model was never triggered, and self-feeding produced two false positives that the same-prompt baseline cannot produce. Cutting the chains to four steps keeps every model-level detection at 100\% precision while using 60\% fewer queries. Needing only text-level query access and a way to recognize malicious output, self-feeding offers a cheap first check on a downloaded model.
tldr: This paper introduces a black-box method to detect backdoors in fine-tuned LLMs by feeding the model's own output back as input.
motivation: Users cannot easily verify the safety of fine-tuned LLMs downloaded from public repositories, as backdoored models behave normally until a trigger is activated.
method: The method, self-feeding, iteratively feeds the model's output back as its next input to drift toward the fine-tuning data, and is tested against a same-prompt baseline on six LLMs with various backdoors.
result: Self-feeding detects backdoors in five of six models at 92.0% pooled precision, while the baseline succeeds on only one of 120 prompt-model pairs; recall per prompt is low but improves at the model level.
conclusion: Self-feeding offers a cheap, black-box first check for backdoors in downloaded LLMs, though it has limitations such as false positives and occasional failures.

title: Welfare Approximation In Multilateral Trade
authors: Tomer Ezra, Aadityan Ganesh, Aviad Rubinstein
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the study of : a mechanism-design problem in which a single potential trade involves [MATH] agents and can be executed only if all [MATH] agents agree to participate. The classical case [MATH] is the well-studied bilateral trade problem, where a seller and a buyer with private values must decide whether to trade an item initially held by the seller. Existing extensions of bilateral trade have largely focused on markets with many buyers and many sellers, but where each realized transaction is still bilateral, requiring agreement only between the matched buyer and seller. Our formulation captures settings in which the trade itself requires joint participation, coupling the agents' incentives and creating new challenges. We study welfare approximation in this setting under incentive compatibility, individual rationality, and budget balance. We give a DSIC mechanism with approximation ratio [MATH], and a BIC mechanism with approximation ratio [MATH]. We prove matching lower bounds up to polylogarithmic factors. Finally, we extend the model to an [MATH]-out-of-[MATH] partial-agreement setting, where the trade may occur once at least [MATH] agents participate. In this relaxed model, the welfare guarantees improve smoothly as [MATH], the number of agents whose participation is not required, grows, and we obtain matching upper and lower bounds up to polylogarithmic factors.
tldr: This paper studies welfare approximation in multilateral trade, a mechanism design problem with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper extends bilateral trade to settings where a trade requires joint participation of multiple agents, creating new incentive challenges.
method: The authors design DSIC and BIC mechanisms with approximation guarantees and prove matching lower bounds, also extending to partial-agreement settings.
result: They achieve approximation ratios with polylogarithmic factors and show smooth improvement in the partial-agreement model.
conclusion: The work contributes to algorithmic mechanism design but is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: A Study Of Kernel Telemetry Options For Security-Oriented Provenance
authors: Paul R. B. Houssel, Olivier Levillain, Sylvie Laniepce, Nicolas Dejon, Herv\'e Debar
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Provenance aims to capture the origins, transformations, and interactions of system objects for security and forensic applications. Existing provenance capture approaches still face major challenges and are not yet ready for production environments. In this paper, we first analyze the main kernel telemetry capture approaches, identifying eBPF as the most promising, and complement this analysis with micro benchmarks to assess its performance overhead and the filtering mechanisms used to achieve capture granularity, such as restricting capture to individual containers. Building on this foundation, we then classify, according to the studied capture approaches and filtering methods, eight provenance systems and five capture agents that could serve as their capture layers, collectively referred to as tools. Our study reveals that these tools are built on highly heterogeneous capture layers, most of which cannot guarantee the integrity and availability of the captured events, completely failing to meet the requirements of security-oriented use cases.
tldr: This paper analyzes kernel telemetry capture approaches for security-oriented provenance, focusing on eBPF and filtering mechanisms, and evaluates eight provenance systems and five capture agents.
motivation: Provenance capture for security and forensics faces challenges and is not production-ready; the paper aims to assess kernel telemetry options to improve capture integrity and availability.
method: The authors analyze main kernel telemetry capture approaches, identify eBPF as most promising, perform micro benchmarks for performance overhead and filtering, and classify eight provenance systems and five capture agents.
result: The study reveals that tools are built on heterogeneous capture layers, most of which cannot guarantee integrity and availability of captured events, failing security-oriented requirements.
conclusion: Current provenance capture tools are not ready for security-oriented use cases; eBPF shows promise but needs further development to meet requirements.

title: Cross-Corpus Evaluation Of Generalizable Vulnerability Detection In IoT Firmware
authors: Sadib Hassan Rumman, Md. Shariful Islam, Md. Rayhanur Rahman
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: IoT firmware vulnerability detection remains challenging due to heterogeneous firmware ecosystems, resource-constrained platforms, and limitations in existing benchmarks. Many datasets are synthetic or general-purpose and lack human-verified, contamination-screened annotations, limiting evidence on cross-corpus generalization across training sources, model architectures, and curriculum strategies. To address this gap, this paper introduces IoTVulBench, a human-verified benchmark for cross-corpus firmware vulnerability detection. IoTVulBench-Core was constructed from GitHub repositories, validated by three expert reviewers, and evaluated on a contamination-screened held-out target across five model architectures, two tuning methods, and three curriculum strategies, with ensemble, distillation, and robustness analyses. Models trained on IoTVulBench achieved the highest MCC among matched single-source datasets, reaching 0.58 versus 0.44 for PrimeVul and 0.39 for D2A. Staged curriculum learning increased MCC to 0.69, while a diversity-optimized ensemble achieved 0.73, improving by 0.42 MCC over the strongest reference comparator, a static analyzer at 0.31, and by 0.29 over PrimeVul. At a 0.5% false-positive rate, the model missed only 21% of vulnerabilities, compared with 71% for the strongest comparator. It retained 86% of its performance under identifier renaming and demonstrated strong calibration and largely faithful explanations. These findings indicate that domain-matched training data and curriculum design, rather than model scale alone, are key drivers of generalization in firmware vulnerability detection. The results provide a benchmark for future research and deployment-ready configurations for practical IoT security applications.
tldr: This paper introduces a benchmark for IoT firmware vulnerability detection, focusing on cross-corpus generalization of machine learning models.
motivation: Existing benchmarks for firmware vulnerability detection are synthetic or lack human verification, limiting evidence on cross-corpus generalization.
method: The authors construct IoTVulBench, a human-verified benchmark, and evaluate multiple model architectures, tuning methods, and curriculum strategies on a contamination-screened target.
result: Models trained on IoTVulBench achieve higher MCC (0.58) than PrimeVul (0.44) and D2A (0.39), with curriculum learning and ensembles improving to 0.69 and 0.73 respectively.
conclusion: Domain-matched training data and curriculum design are key drivers of generalization in firmware vulnerability detection, providing a benchmark for future research.

title: Strengthening Full Justified Representation: Efficient Verification And Computation
authors: Nicholas Teh
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Full justified representation (FJR) is among the strongest known satisfiable proportionality axioms for approval-based committee elections. Recent work has shown that an FJR committee can be found in polynomial time, but verifying whether a given committee satisfies FJR remains coNP-complete. We introduce FJR+, a strict strengthening of FJR and EJR+ that can be verified and satisfied in polynomial time. We then analyze the Residual-Budget Greedy (RBG) algorithm and prove that it selects a partial committee such that every size-[MATH] completion satisfies FJR+. This freedom allows us to use sequential Phragm\'en to obtain a priceable completion. The resulting rule always satisfies FJR+ and the sub-core, and it is priceable whenever at least [MATH] candidates receive an approval. We also obtain a Droop-quota version of FJR+. Finally, we extend FJR+ to approval-based participatory budgeting with arbitrary project costs. A project-specific version of RBG computes this property in polynomial time and can be continued to a priceable outcome satisfying a cost-based version of the sub-core.
tldr: This paper introduces FJR+, a strengthened proportionality axiom for approval-based committee elections, and provides efficient algorithms for verification and computation.
motivation: The paper addresses computational challenges in verifying full justified representation (FJR) in committee elections, which is coNP-complete.
method: The authors define FJR+, a stricter axiom that is polynomial-time verifiable, and analyze the Residual-Budget Greedy (RBG) algorithm to show it yields committees satisfying FJR+.
result: They prove that RBG selects a partial committee such that every completion satisfies FJR+, and extend the results to participatory budgeting with costs.
conclusion: The work provides a practical strengthening of FJR with efficient algorithms, but it is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Plaintext Recovery Against Post-Filtering Access Control
authors: David Cash Zachary Espiritu (mongodb Research)
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fine-grained access control (FGAC) mechanisms such as row-level security (RLS) and document-level security (DLS) are widely deployed in databases to restrict access to data stored in physical indexing structures shared by multiple users (e.g., in multi-tenant databases, or in the implementation of least-privilege within an organization). FGAC implementations often use post-filtering where untrusted queries run over all data and private results are redacted afterwards. Prior work shows this approach can lead to side-channels that enable attackers to test if a chosen value exists in unseen data. While damaging, prior attacks do not enable the efficient recovery of rich, high-entropy data like full records or text documents. We show these side-channels are more damaging than previously thought. Using rich query interfaces (e.g., range, prefix, and conjunctive predicates), we amplify existence leakage into reconstruction attacks. We do this in two settings: - PostgreSQL (RLS timing). We exploit a timing side-channel and expressive SQL queries (e.g., ranges, conjunctions) to enumerate unknown attribute values and, in turn, full records via binary search over large domains. - Elasticsearch/OpenSearch (DLS scoring). We exploit scoring and prefix-expansion side-channels to recover indexed terms from documents. In some cases, we can extract [MATH]-grams in the corpus to recover approximate text. Our results show that FGAC side-channels must be evaluated in the presence of rich predicates, which can turn membership tests into scalable reconstruction of high-entropy records.
tldr: This paper presents reconstruction attacks against fine-grained access control systems by exploiting side-channels in post-filtering, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The paper addresses security vulnerabilities in database access control, which is a classical computer security topic, not quantum information.
method: The authors demonstrate attacks using timing and scoring side-channels in PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch to recover high-entropy data.
result: They show that side-channels can be amplified into full record reconstruction, posing a serious threat to data confidentiality.
conclusion: The findings highlight the need for careful evaluation of side-channels in access control systems, but the work is outside the scope of the user's research interests.

title: Towards Model-based Run-time Cybersecurity: On Control-Flow Anomaly Detection, Attack Identification, And Hardware Monitoring
authors: Martin Sachenbacher, Martin Leucker, Alexander Weiss, Aliyu Tanko Ali
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Methods to increase the resilience of systems to cyber-attacks become increasingly important. Control-flow monitoring provides a principled basis to ensure integrity and detect possible anomalies at run-time. Once anomalies have been detected, so-called attack trees can be used to identify possible types of attacks. However, this approach is vulnerable to camouflage, by which attackers try to evade detection (and correct identification) by deliberately manipulating also the system's observed control flow. In this paper, we outline a model-based approach that provides more robust intrusion detection and attack identification through an architecture that combines software- with hardware-based monitoring. In this approach, software-level observation indicates suspicious activities, while hardware-level monitoring checks them separately in more detail, making it much harder for attacks to camouflage themselves and go undetected. We illustrate the approach with an authentication-service example that captures a realistic failure mode: a software-level observer sees an anomalous but apparently harmless control-flow deviation, maps it to a benign root cause in an attack tree, but misses the true intrusion. A second, independent hardware control-flow monitor observes the actual transition sequence and thereby changes the attack-tree diagnosis from a low-severity configuration or maintenance issue to a high-confidence code-injection or control-flow hijack. In this scenario, the proposed combination of control-flow anomaly detection, attack-tree based intrusion identification, and hardware-based monitoring can improve not only anomaly detection, but also the diagnostic precision of attack-tree-based cyber-attack identification.
tldr: This paper proposes a model-based cybersecurity approach combining software and hardware monitoring for control-flow anomaly detection and attack identification.
motivation: To improve resilience against cyber-attacks by detecting control-flow anomalies and identifying attack types, while addressing the vulnerability of camouflage.
method: The approach integrates software-level observation with independent hardware-level monitoring to cross-check suspicious activities, using attack trees for diagnosis.
result: The combination improves anomaly detection and diagnostic precision, as illustrated in an authentication-service example where hardware monitoring reveals a high-confidence code-injection attack.
conclusion: The proposed architecture enhances intrusion detection and attack identification robustness against camouflage.

title: How China-Origin Vision-Language Models Move From Refusal To Reframing In State Alignment
authors: Guang Yang, Fengchen Liu, Alex Wang, Homa Hosseinmardi, Amir Ghasemian
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: State-aligned distortion has been documented in China-origin text-based large language models (LLMs), but whether, and in what form, it arises in multimodal systems has not been systematically examined. We construct a balanced benchmark of 200 core entries spanning ten politically sensitive topics, plus a seven-variant visual-abstraction probe, and run nine vision-language models (VLMs), seven China-origin and two non-China, across four elicitation paradigms and two prompt languages, yielding 21,708 trials. Each response is audited on six dimensions -- explicit refusal, information integrity, visual grounding, state-aligned framing, language consistency, and response length -- by two independent frontier LLM judges, validated against three human experts on a 200-trial sample. Measuring each dimension separately lets us decompose multimodal censorship into individual signals rather than a single refusal-based score; in particular, refusal and framing are measured independently, so a model can stop refusing while still reframing. We find that (i) Chinese-language prompting roughly triples the odds of state-aligned framing, within every model; (ii) China-origin models reframe more than non-China models (direction robust across judges and human raters; magnitude 1.6--3.2x); (iii) the effect is strongest in text-only political commentary (36.5%) and is gated by recognition of the depicted subject rather than pixel detail, persisting even at silhouette for iconic images; and (iv) across four Qwen generations, state-aligned framing rises while explicit refusal falls: censorship migrates from a visible act (refusal) to an invisible one (fluent reframing). We argue this shift to invisible reframing is fundamentally a problem of human-AI interaction: it removes the very signal users rely on to recognize that information has been withheld.
tldr: This paper studies state-aligned censorship in China-origin vision-language models, finding a shift from explicit refusal to fluent reframing.
motivation: To systematically examine whether state-aligned distortion, previously documented in text-based LLMs, also appears in multimodal systems and to decompose censorship into individual signals.
method: Constructed a benchmark of 200 politically sensitive topics with visual variants, ran nine VLMs across four elicitation paradigms and two languages, and audited responses on six dimensions using LLM judges and human validation.
result: Chinese-language prompting triples state-aligned framing; China-origin models reframe 1.6-3.2x more; effect is strongest in text-only commentary and persists even at silhouette; across Qwen generations, framing rises while refusal falls.
conclusion: Censorship in VLMs is migrating from visible refusal to invisible reframing, posing a challenge for users to detect information withholding.

title: ToolHazard: Scaling Adversarial Environments For Security Evaluation And Alignment Of LLM-based Agents
authors: Yutao Mou, Pengfei Yang, Zhe Yin, Zhangchi Xue, Xiaotian Luan, Dingyao Yu, Tong Zhang, Shikun Zhang, Wei Ye
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents integrated with external tools are vulnerable to indirect prompt injections embedded in environmental states. However, existing studies largely rely on manually implemented or reused environments, stochastic LLM-based tool simulation, and predefined injection locations, limiting scalable security research across broader domains. To bridge this gap, we propose **ToolHazard**, a scalable adversarial environment synthesis framework that reduces human engineering and supports expansion with additional seed domains and compute. Through an Environment Simulator, an Attacker Agent, and a User Simulator, ToolHazard synthesizes executable stateful environments, discovers viable injection points and generates environment-specific payloads, and constructs state-grounded long-horizon tasks. Based on ToolHazard, we build **ToolHazard-Bench** for stress-testing agents under complex workflows and diverse environmental attacks. Experiments reveal substantial agent vulnerabilities and show that injection timing and placement affect attack effectiveness. Moreover, ToolHazard-generated alignment data improves security on both ToolHazard-Bench and AgentDojo while preserving benign task utility.
tldr: This paper introduces ToolHazard, a framework for generating adversarial environments to evaluate and improve the security of LLM-based agents against indirect prompt injections.
motivation: Existing security evaluations of LLM agents rely on manual or limited environments, hindering scalable research across domains.
method: ToolHazard uses an Environment Simulator, Attacker Agent, and User Simulator to synthesize executable stateful environments, discover injection points, generate payloads, and construct long-horizon tasks.
result: Experiments show significant agent vulnerabilities, with injection timing and placement affecting attack success, and alignment data from ToolHazard improves security on benchmarks while preserving utility.
conclusion: ToolHazard provides a scalable approach for security evaluation and alignment of LLM agents, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Comparing Call-by-Name And Call-by-Value Reduction And Reduction Strategies In Calculi For Classical Logic
authors: David Davies Steffen van Bakel
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define call-by-name and call-by-value reduction and reduction strategies for the calculi slmu (symmetric lmu), lmmt, and Xs (X with implicit substitution). We establish a strong relation between these notions through defining a single interpretation from slmu to lmmt that respects normal reduction, as well as the call-by-name and call-by-value reduction in slmu within the their counterpart in lmmt; for the strategies, we will show similar, but weaker results. We also define a single mapping from lmmt to Xs, and show that this also respects all three notions. We then continue with studying the natural encoding of Xs into lmmt, and show that only full reduction is respected, but that reduction steps are needed to model substitution, so the CBN and CBV strategies cannot be respected. We conclude with studying the combination of our efforts and define an interpretation of slmu into Xs, and show that CBN and CBV reduction are respected. This result underlines that Xs and lmmt are similar, but different calculi, and that the nature of slmu makes that any encoding into either can never fully respect the strategies.
tldr: This paper studies reduction strategies in calculi for classical logic, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The paper aims to compare call-by-name and call-by-value reduction in several calculi for classical logic, motivated by theoretical computer science interests.
method: The authors define reduction relations and strategies for slmu, lmmt, and Xs, and establish mappings between them to compare the reductions.
result: They show that certain mappings respect reduction notions, but strategies are not fully respected due to the nature of the calculi.
conclusion: The work clarifies the relationships between these calculi, but has no connection to the user's research areas.

title: Slips: Behavioral Evidence Aggregation For Network Security
authors: Sebastian Garcia, Veronica Valeros, Alya Gomaa, Ond\v{r}ej Luk\'a\v{s}, Martin \v{r}epa, Luk\'a\v{s} Forst, David Otta, Franti\v{s}ek St\v{r}as\'ak, Jan Svoboda, Dita Hollmannov\'a
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11979v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Network intrusion detection systems often analyze individual packets or flows, although malicious behavior may develop across many connections and over time. This may limit their ability to combine isolated detections into a coherent assessment of host behavior. Packet-level features may also be too low-level for complex AI-based detection, requiring additional processing to improve accuracy while maintaining a low false-positive rate. We present Slips, a network intrusion detection system that builds host-centered behavioral profiles and organizes activity into time windows. It uses a modular architecture in which independent modules report evidence rather than generating final alerts directly. Slips then accumulates this evidence into host-level decisions. We evaluate Slips against Suricata on an expert-labeled PCAP dataset. At the profile-time-window level, Slips achieved 83% higher recall and a 70% higher F1 score than Suricata, while neither system produced false positives. These results indicate that time-window-based evidence accumulation can produce context-aware decisions that better align with expert judgment.
tldr: This paper presents Slips, a network intrusion detection system that aggregates behavioral evidence over time windows to improve detection accuracy.
motivation: Traditional network intrusion detection systems analyze individual packets or flows, missing malicious behavior that spans multiple connections. The authors aim to improve detection by building host-centered behavioral profiles and accumulating evidence over time.
method: Slips uses a modular architecture where independent modules report evidence, which is then aggregated into host-level decisions over time windows. It was evaluated against Suricata on an expert-labeled PCAP dataset.
result: Slips achieved 83% higher recall and 70% higher F1 score than Suricata at the profile-time-window level, with no false positives from either system.
conclusion: Time-window-based evidence accumulation can produce context-aware decisions that better align with expert judgment in network security.

title: Tolls For Dynamic Equilibrium Flows
authors: Lukas Graf, Tobias Harks, Julian Schwarz
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider dynamic network flows and study the following question: Which dynamic edge flows can be implemented as tolled dynamic equilibrium flows? We study this question for the heterogeneous-user model, where the flow particles are partitioned into populations characterized by their own source,destination-pairs and a cost function associating with any walk and departure time some costs. As our two main results, we first provide a duality-based characterization of implementability of dynamic edge flows for the multi-source, multi-destination case. Secondly, we derive both, a combinatorial and duality-based characterization of implementability of dynamic edge flows for the multi-source, single-destination case. Both results are derived under a fairly general network loading model. For the proof, we make several technical contributions: We formulate a novel infinite dimensional optimization problem, where the goal is to minimize the aggregated costs of the particles with respect to the fixed network loading induced by the given edge flow. This requires the recently introduced concept of autonomous network loadings for which we show several new structural insights. In particular, we give an alternative (tighter) characterization of the existence of autonomous network loadings for our setting by deriving a generalization of a result of M.A. Zarecki on the Lusin [MATH] property of absolutely continuous monotone functions which may also be of independent interest. These insights allow us to prove the stated characterizations under the assumption of strong duality. Finally, for the case of a single-destination, we are able to provide a non-trivial proof that this assumption is always fulfilled for finitely supported edge flows with costs representing weighted travel times.
tldr: This paper studies tolled dynamic equilibrium flows in transportation networks, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper addresses a question in transportation network theory: which dynamic edge flows can be implemented as tolled equilibrium flows. This is a classical optimization and game theory problem.
method: The authors use duality-based characterizations and combinatorial arguments, introducing an infinite-dimensional optimization problem and leveraging autonomous network loadings and a generalization of Zarecki's theorem.
result: They provide characterizations of implementability for multi-source multi-destination and multi-source single-destination cases under general network loading models.
conclusion: The work contributes to transportation science and mathematical optimization, but has no connection to the user's research interests in quantum information and related fields.

title: The Optimal Discounting Parameter Of The Power Prior Under Predictive Log-Loss
authors: Yuriy A. Reznik
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The power prior of Ibrahim and Chen incorporates historical data into a Bayesian analysis by raising the historical likelihood to a power [MATH]. The choice of the exponent has remained an open question. This paper gives a closed-form answer under the predictive log-loss. For a model with [MATH] parameters, a historical sample of size [MATH], and average Kullback--Leibler divergence [MATH] between the historical and current data-generating distributions, the optimal exponent is [MATH]. Equivalently, the optimally borrowed effective sample size obeys the harmonic law [MATH]: compatible data are pooled in full, and any difference caps the borrowed information at [MATH] observations. The result is exact for multinomial data and extends to smooth parametric families. The law benchmarks adaptive borrowing, explains the reported degeneracy of the normalized power prior, and shows that neither subsetting the data nor decaying the exponent improves on the correctly discounted constant.
tldr: This paper derives the optimal discounting parameter for the power prior under predictive log-loss, yielding a harmonic law for effective sample size borrowing.
motivation: The choice of the power prior exponent has been an open question in Bayesian analysis, and this work aims to provide a principled answer.
method: The author analytically optimizes the predictive log-loss to find the optimal exponent, deriving a closed-form solution for multinomial data and extending to smooth parametric families.
result: The optimal exponent leads to a harmonic law: compatible data are fully pooled, while any difference caps borrowed information at a fixed number of observations.
conclusion: The result provides a benchmark for adaptive borrowing and explains the degeneracy of the normalized power prior, showing that subsetting or decaying the exponent is not beneficial.

title: Machine Learning-Based Cyber Defense For Cloud Infrastructure: An Adaptive Deep Q-Network Architecture For Intelligent Intrusion Detection And Automated Threat Mitigation
authors: Md Yassir Mottalib, Md Yousuf, Eklachur Rahman Bhuiyan, S M Ahsan Habib, Sonjoy Kumar Dey, Md. Salahuddin Gazi, Molay Kumar Roy, Asaduzzaman Anik
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the increasing complexity of cyber assaults in cloud environments, adaptable security solutions are needed that can support real-time detection and autonomous response. In this paper, we propose a reinforcement learning-based dynamic cyber defense framework. We deploy a Deep Q-Network (DQN) to train effective defensive strategies to counteract the evolving cyberattacks. We leverage the CICIDS2017 dataset for model creation and the UNSW-NB15 dataset for external validation, involving preprocessing of data, feature engineering, and adaptive policy learning. We compare the proposed DQN with decision tree, support vector machine, random forest, XGBoost, and multilayer perceptron models. The proposed DQN achieves an accuracy of 99.72%, a precision of 99.68%, a recall of 99.65%, an F1-score of 99.66%, and an ROC-AUC of 0.999, while the false positive rate is 0.31%, the false negative rate is 0.35%, and the detection latency is 15 ms. The framework achieved 99.54% attack mitigation rate, demonstrating strong adaptive and real-time defensive capabilities. These results demonstrate the potential of reinforcement learning as a powerful and scalable approach for autonomous cybersecurity in modern cloud environments.
tldr: This paper applies a Deep Q-Network for intrusion detection and threat mitigation in cloud environments, achieving high accuracy and low latency.
motivation: The increasing complexity of cyberattacks in cloud environments necessitates adaptive security solutions that can detect and respond in real time.
method: The authors propose a reinforcement learning-based framework using a Deep Q-Network (DQN) trained on the CICIDS2017 dataset and validated on UNSW-NB15, comparing it with traditional machine learning models.
result: The DQN achieves 99.72% accuracy, 99.68% precision, 99.65% recall, 99.66% F1-score, 0.999 ROC-AUC, 0.31% false positive rate, 0.35% false negative rate, 15 ms detection latency, and 99.54% attack mitigation rate.
conclusion: The results demonstrate that reinforcement learning is a powerful and scalable approach for autonomous cybersecurity in cloud environments.

title: Deciding Amalgamation Beyond Arity Two: The Semantic Horn Case
authors: Jakub Rydval
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12206v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the amalgamation decision problem: given a universal first-order sentence [MATH], decide whether the class [MATH] of its finite models has the amalgamation property. We call [MATH] semantic Horn if [MATH] is closed under binary direct products. By McKinsey's theorem, this is equivalent to [MATH] being logically equivalent to a universal Horn sentence; the distinction is one of input representation, since [MATH] itself need not be given in Horn form and conversion to an explicit Horn normal form can incur an exponential blow-up. We prove that the problem is decidable under this semantic promise. Moreover, it belongs to 2EXPTIME, and to EXPTIME for every fixed bound on the arity of the input signature. Thus the semantic Horn fragment admits an unconditional decision procedure for signatures of unbounded relational arity. Our proof starts from the inside-out correspondence, which we use as a black box for the semantic reduction to a finite completion problem. We encode finite completions as homomorphisms to a finite relational template and introduce a finite set-valued local-consistency certificate for completion problems whose template has bounded width. For semantic Horn inputs, the local completions over each fixed source chart are closed under relationwise intersection of the added relations, and these intersections are compatible with restriction maps. This yields a semilattice polymorphism of the completion template. Since the template is binary, the semilattice operation gives width [MATH], making the local-consistency certificate complete. The same construction gives a decision procedure whenever the associated completion template has bounded width.
tldr: This paper studies the decidability of the amalgamation property for universal first-order sentences under a semantic Horn condition, a topic in model theory and logic.
motivation: The amalgamation property is a fundamental concept in model theory, and the paper aims to determine if it is decidable for a broad class of finite structures under a semantic promise.
method: The proof uses the inside-out correspondence to reduce the problem to a finite completion problem, encodes completions as homomorphisms to a finite relational template, and introduces a local-consistency certificate based on semilattice polymorphisms.
result: The problem is decidable in 2EXPTIME, and in EXPTIME for fixed arity signatures, providing an unconditional decision procedure for unbounded relational arity.
conclusion: The semantic Horn fragment of the amalgamation decision problem is decidable, contributing to the understanding of model-theoretic properties.

title: VICBench: A Multi-Language Benchmark For Code Vulnerability Detection
authors: Jin Lu, Xuening Han, Yang Zhong, Lin Tan, Kevin Luo, Andrew Gacek, Neha Rungta
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating security vulnerability detection tools requires benchmark datasets with vulnerability-inducing commits (VICs) - the commits that first introduce vulnerabilities into codebases. VICs are essential for determining the full range of vulnerable software versions. Existing vulnerability datasets suffer from limited programming language coverage, restricted patch complexity, and narrow project scope. Through our dual annotation by human experts and an agentic workflow, we create a benchmark - VICBench - of 100 verified VICs for 100 CVEs across 88 projects in Python, Java, and C++, covering 48 CWE types. VICBench features complex real-world vulnerability fixes averaging 38.6 lines and corresponding VICs of 252.5 lines - significantly larger than prior work. Our evaluation shows that state-of-the-art algorithms V-SZZ and LLM4SZZ achieve only 33.3%-40.1% F1, confirming that using existing approaches still entails significant manual effort. VICBench enables robust evaluation of vulnerability detection approaches.
tldr: This paper introduces VICBench, a multi-language benchmark for code vulnerability detection, which is unrelated to quantum information science.
motivation: The paper addresses the need for better benchmarks in software security, specifically for vulnerability-inducing commits, but this is outside the scope of the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems.
method: The authors created VICBench by collecting 100 verified vulnerability-inducing commits across Python, Java, and C++, using human expert annotation and an agentic workflow, and evaluated state-of-the-art algorithms.
result: The benchmark includes 100 VICs for 100 CVEs across 88 projects and 48 CWE types, with larger patch sizes than prior work, and existing algorithms achieve only 33.3%-40.1% F1.
conclusion: VICBench provides a more challenging and comprehensive benchmark for vulnerability detection, but it is not relevant to the user's research areas.

title: Convergent Detour Hijacking: Task-Preserving Resource Amplification In Skill-Based Llm Agents
authors: Junliang Liu, Ruoyu Li, Wenxin Tang, Jingyu Xiao, Zhenyu Liu, Jingheng Xu, Laizhong Cui
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on third-party skills, using natural-language descriptions for selection and instruction bodies for planning. This progressive-disclosure design exposes two sequential control points to untrusted publishers: a static skill may steer an otherwise correct task onto an unnecessarily costly trajectory. Prior work studies selection manipulation, malicious skill instructions, and tool-chain resource amplification largely separately, leaving their end-to-end composition unclear. We introduce Convergent Detour Hijacking (CDH), a text-only, runtime-independent attack that couples these stages. Under shared semantic cover, a description establishes relevance during selection, while an aligned body reuses that rationale to fabricate plausible dependencies during planning. CDH attracts an attacker-controlled coordinator alongside legitimate skills, recruits unnecessary benign skills into a bounded detour, and then re-enters the original route to preserve task completion. We evaluate it across multiple LLM backends and 491 held-out tasks under single-task and multi-turn conditions. On DeepSeek-V4-Pro, the matched coordinator is selected in 80.02% of tasks; among coordinator-hit runs that complete tasks, token consumption and end-to-end execution time increase by 66.91% and 92.45%, respectively, while aggregate task completion remains comparable. Thus, correct outcomes do not guarantee trajectory integrity or cost safety.
tldr: This paper introduces Convergent Detour Hijacking, a security attack on LLM agents that exploits skill descriptions and instructions to amplify resource consumption while preserving task completion.
motivation: LLM agents increasingly rely on third-party skills, and prior work has studied selection manipulation, malicious instructions, and resource amplification separately, leaving their composition unclear.
method: The attack couples description-based selection manipulation with instruction-based planning manipulation to attract an attacker-controlled coordinator, recruit benign skills into a detour, and then re-enter the original route.
result: On DeepSeek-V4-Pro, the matched coordinator is selected in 80.02% of tasks, and among coordinator-hit runs, token consumption and execution time increase by 66.91% and 92.45% respectively, while task completion remains comparable.
conclusion: Correct outcomes do not guarantee trajectory integrity or cost safety, highlighting a new security vulnerability in LLM agent systems.

title: Preservation And Definability For The Fluted Fragment
authors: Yiwen Ding
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12970v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper investigates preservation and definability for the equality-free fluted fragment over finite relational signatures. We first prove an equirank homomorphism preservation theorem: every homomorphism-preserved fluted sentence has an existential-positive fluted equivalent of no greater quantifier rank. We then refute Purdy's claimed Los--Tarski preservation theorem for the fluted fragment. Our counterexample is a rank-three sentence over one binary relation that is preserved under extensions but has no existential fluted equivalent. Finally, a two-variable counterexample over a unary base signature shows that weak and ordinary Beth definability both fail. All three results hold over all structures and over finite structures.
tldr: This paper studies preservation and definability theorems for the fluted fragment of first-order logic, a topic in mathematical logic with no connection to quantum information.
motivation: The paper aims to settle open questions about the fluted fragment, a decidable fragment of first-order logic, specifically regarding homomorphism preservation and Beth definability.
method: The author proves an equirank homomorphism preservation theorem and constructs counterexamples to refute a claimed Los-Tarski theorem and to show failure of Beth definability.
result: The paper establishes a homomorphism preservation theorem for the fluted fragment, refutes Purdy's claimed preservation theorem, and provides counterexamples for Beth definability.
conclusion: The results contribute to the model theory of the fluted fragment but are entirely unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
